News.title: UK seaside town will celebrate Christmas TOMORROW with Santa on the beach, festive music and grotto
News.content:
A SEASIDE resort town is preparing to celebrate Christmas on the beach tomorrow (August 5) as part of an unusual tradition.

Locals have been encouraged to put on a Christmas jumper and a pair of flip flops for a day of carolling and ice creams.



Residents of Bridlington, on the East Yorkshire coastline, are set to celebrate Christmas tomorrow in a packed programme of festive entertainment.

Known as “Bridmas Day”, the jam-packed day of activities is organised by East Riding of Yorkshire council to promote the town as an all-year-round destination.



A cabinet member for the council, Nick Coultish, said Bridmas Day has become “one of the highlights of Bridlington’s events calendar”.

Throughout the day, families will be able to buy goodies at the Christmas Market, enjoy their favourite festive music, and watch a showing of The Grinch.



Children can even meet Santa at his summertime grotto on Bridlington South Beach, where a Christmas tree will be put up to mark the occasion.

Local businesses are expected to take part in the celebrations by dressing up their stores in Christmas decorations.

For Bridlington, the festivities mark the beginning of its seasonal offers launch, where locals can snap up prizes and exclusive offers for a number different winter activities.

These include a family day pass to the historic country house Sewerby Hall and Gardens, tickets on the Santa Express, and two tickets to see a Shania Twain tribute act at Bridlington Spa on Friday night.



Visitors can also secure a 10 per cent discount for the local Pantomine of Cinderella, starring Celebrity Big Brother winner, David Potts.

Despite the positivity from East Riding of Yorkshire council, who have counted down the days with 12 Days of Christmas posts, others are more sceptical.

One local said: “Come on guys. Let’s enjoy our lovely summer holidays without being reminded of Christmas just yet.”



Bridmas Day will be celebrated in Bridlington Spa from 10am to 4pm tomorrow, with a number of free events on offer.

News.title: Man, 35, arrested on suspicion of murder after beloved dad, 36, shot dead at UK traveller site as family pay tribute
News.content:
MURDER ARREST Man, 35, arrested on suspicion of murder after beloved dad, 36, shot dead at UK traveller site as family pay tribute

A MAN has been arrested following the alleged fatal shooting of a “much-loved” husband and father.

Jimmy Ward, 36, was pronounced dead at Calcutt traveller site near Cricklade, Wiltshire, on Sunday morning.



A 35-year-old man has been arrested today on suspicion of murder after Jimmy was shot dead.

Wiltshire Police have said that a total of five people have been arrested in connection with Jimmy’s death.



Two other men, aged 53 and 29, were arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender following a vehicle stop on the A419 road today.

On Sunday, a 74-year-old man and 42-year-old woman were arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender and possession of a firearm.



All five people are in custody for questioning, police confirmed.

Tributes have poured in, with people leaving flowers and cards at the traveller site.



One mourner wrote: “RIP to my daughter-in-law’s dad Jimmy Ward. Please everyone pray for all the family, my heart goes out to them all.

“Very hard to believe. Rest in heavenly peace my cousin Jimmy Ward,” added another.”

“Thinking of all the family and friends at this very sad time, sending lots of love to his wife and children. Far too young to die, rest in peace,” said another local.

Others have described him as “a gentleman”.

It’s believed Jimmy leaves behind a wife and children.



Senior Investigating Officer Detective Chief Inspector Phil Walker said: “This is a significant development in our investigation.

“I can confirm that a man has been arrested on suspicion of Jimmy’s murder and is now in police custody, along with four other people on suspicion of assisting an offender.

“Jimmy’s next of kin have been informed of this development and my thoughts continue to be with them.

“They are being supported by specially trained officers.

“A scene and heavy policing presence remain in place at the traveller site in Calcutt while further inquiries are carried out. I continue to ask that this cordon is respected.

“I’d like to thank the local community for their support and patience since Sunday.

“We understand this incident has caused significant concern, so please consider speaking with officers about any information or concerns you may have.”

News.title: Inexplicable decision to free thugs who killed PC Harper is final betrayal – it’s an insult to us all, says police chief
News.content:
NO police officer will forget where they were on that summer’s night in 2019 when the radio call came through about the death of our colleague PC Andrew Harper.

Harps had been brutally killed.



Dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

His injuries were catastrophic.



Nor will we forget the faces of Andrew’s smirking killers – Henry Long, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers – as they attended the Old Bailey to be found guilty of his manslaughter.

These low lifes showed no remorse. They offered no apology.

Equally, neither will we forget the Government’s inexplicable and unforgivable decision to allow those who kill police officers to be released early from jail.

It is a final betrayal from the politicians, who are supposed to be on our side.

A smack in the face to every one of us police officers across the United Kingdom, who are out there now risking our lives to keep you, the public, safe.

I am absolutely outraged that Justice Secretary Alex Norris, and Prime Minister Andy Burnham, have decided that killing a police officer in the execution of their duty is somehow less serious than other offences deemed too dangerous for early release.



Both said they wanted to do more to stop the release of two of the young men convicted of killing Harps after serving just 40 per cent of their 13-year tariffs.

They may have claimed they wanted to do more but facts matter. They did not.

Let me be clear now, on behalf of thousands of Thames Valley Police Officers.



I challenge the Prime Minister and Justice Secretary to stand before Andrew’s widow, Lissie, his parents, his brother, his loved ones, or indeed any police officer in this country.

Stand before them and explain why those responsible for killing a police officer should still be eligible for early release.

Try telling the officers who attended the scene where Andrew died on 15 August 2019 and witnessed the horrific consequences of that crime.

And the friends and colleagues who had to hear about Andrew’s death on their radio.

Explain to them why the life of a police officer does not warrant the same protection as other serious crimes under this legislation.



This decision pours salt into wounds that have never healed.

It is an insult to Andrew’s family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family.

Time and again they have been forced to relive their grief while watching a justice system that they trusted, fail to recognise the unique sacrifice made by those who serve and protect the public.



We stood side by side with Lissie as she successfully campaigned for Harper’s Law in Andrew’s name following their pitiful manslaughter sentences these three teenagers received.

As a result of the campaign, those who kill emergency service workers now receive mandatory life sentences.

If Andrew’s killers were convicted today, they would receive life sentences due to the law that was created in his name.

They would not be eligible for early release.

I completely agree that rapists and child sexual offenders should not be released early from their sentences.



However, you cannot say in the next breath that people who kill people – and in particular police officers out there protecting society – can be subject to that release.

It’s perverse to say that, and it does not make sense. And that’s what I need to understand.

So what next?



We will throw everything at this through a proper legal challenge from KCs, barristers, you name it. Our colleagues will accept nothing less.

This decision is totally demoralising for all police officers and our fellow emergency service workers, who put themselves in harm’s way to protect and serve their community.

And not just in Thames Valley, but right across the country.

We will do what we have to do to protect Andrew Harper’s legacy and other victims up and down the country who don’t have a platform to put their points across on radio, television and in newspapers.

Because make no mistake there are silent victims, families and loved ones of other individuals who have been killed, who will also be outraged at this.



Police officers put themselves in harm’s way every day.

They run towards danger when everyone else is running away.

They do so knowing that they may never come home to their families.



For the Government to exclude the killers of police officers from these protections sends a deeply troubling message about the value placed on those who make that sacrifice.

Andrew Harper’s family deserved better. Every police officer in this country deserves better.

I will not stand by while the voices of Andrew’s family, his colleagues and police officers across this country continue to be ignored.

We will take this to Parliament. We will not stop. Andy Burnham may be on his holidays but we won’t rest on this.

And you can help us.



We have launched a petition – Stop the early release from jail of PC Andrew Harper’s killers – and would encourage all right-minded members of the public to please sign and share this link.

We will be working hard with both local and national politicians to right this wrong.

How dare ministers say the killing of a police officer is not serious enough to merit the stiffest of punishments.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you kill a police officer there should be no early release. No ifs. No buts.

Somebody, somewhere, must finally listen.

News.title: Severed heads & bombs as wedding gifts… ISIS breeding ground minutes from Ceuta with new migrant invasion feared in days
News.content:
A MOROCCAN town next to Spanish enclave Ceuta that saw an influx of migrants last week is an ISIS breeding ground once home to a terrorist brute who posed with severed heads and gifted his bride a bomb belt.

The border town of Fnideq, which hosts 85,000 inhabitants and is known in Spanish as Castillejos, is the closest Moroccan urban centre to Ceuta.



It comes amid fears another invasion of Ceuta – where 70,000 migrants crossed the border on Thursday – could happen again in the coming days.

Fnideq is a primary recruitment hub for Islamic State extremists in North Africa.



In 2015, at the height of the Syrian conflict, it was estimated around 400 of the 1,200 Moroccans who had travelled to Syria and Iraq to join ISIS came from Fnideq.

One of them, Mohamed Hamdouch, became notorious for posing with the severed heads of his victims – and was known as The Decapitator.



In one image that appeared on jihadist forums he held a bloody knife in his hand and showed off the severed heads of five Syrian soldiers.

The Moroccan ISIS fighter, also known as Kokito Castillejos, gained notoriety in Spain for marrying a woman from Ceuta and giving her an explosive belt as a wedding gift.



He was killed while fighting in Syria in November 2015.

Many Islamic extremists have snuck into Spain as irregular migrants in the past before going on to be arrested or linked to terror.

This includes former rapper-turned-jihadist Abdel-Majed Abdel-Bary, who was raised in Maida Vale, West London.



The dual British-Egyptian national quit his music career to join ISIS in Syria in 2013, quickly becoming one of the group’s most infamous British faces.

He sparked horror after posting a picture holding the severed head of a Syrian soldier, captioned: “Chillin’ with my homie, or what’s left of him.”

The image even led to him being briefly misidentified as ISIS executioner “Jihadi John”.



After fleeing ISIS, Abdel-Bary sneaked into Spain by migrant boat from Algeria in April 2020 alongside two accomplices – Abderrazak Seddiki, 31, and Kossaila Chollouah, 28.

All three were arrested in a hideout in Almería.

While his two companions were later convicted of terror offenses, Abdel-Bary was found dead in his Cadiz prison cell in July 2023, just days into his Madrid trial.

Some 70,000 people swam from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta located in North Africa on Thursday – with dramatic images and videos showing the chaos unfold.

There are fears another mass border crossing is being planned in the coming days – as social media posts calling for a second invasion gain traction.



Reports say the peninsula could see scenes of mayhem play out on the streets yet again, as plans are being made for another mass border crossing on August 15.

On social media, posts appear to be plotting another storming of the shores of Ceuta, with one message reading: “Everything will be seen that day.”

Another appears to call for the creation of a WhatsApp group, saying: “Our appointment is on 15/08/2026.”

Migrants desperate to try to reach Europe are reportedly being encouraged to join the group by sending a private message using the password “Ceuta”.

The revelation of the messages and posts – written in Darija, an Arabic dialect spoken in Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia – has sparked major concern in Ceuta.



It also comes after Spanish cops claimed today at least a dozen convicted terrorists were among those who went across the border last week.

Terrorists previously deported to Morocco after arrests in Spain were part of the mass crossing, local outlet El Espanol reported.

Authorities believe it is “very possible” the number of criminals with links to Islamic extremists could increase.

The Spanish territory is still reeling from the “apocalyptic” scenes last week.

Up to 70,000 migrants were believed to have entered the city during the frenzied ordeal.



Over 48,000 have been frogmarched back across the frontier by Spanish cops and military personnel.

But there are currently an estimated 5,000 migrants, including nearly 1,000 children, remaining in the Spanish territory trying to dodge the security sweep.

Distressing pictures have shown dozens of North African youths sleeping on the pavement on makeshift beds made out of cardboard boxes.

The children will most likely end up being transferred to the Spanish mainland to ease overcrowding in Ceuta.

The city is already caring for some 850 children, but is planning to expand its facilities with two more centres, as the number of youngsters is expected to rise over the coming days.



Fights broke out on Monday during the first Red Cross handout of food and drinks at Trampolin Beach.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Several police clashes also erupted last week amid the chaos, and at least 72 people were killed due to drowning or the resulting beach stampede after the migrants crossed into the Spanish territory.

News.title: Surrogate mom fights to save baby she is carrying as biological parents push for ABORTION over treatable heart condition
News.content:
BATTLE FOR LIFE Surrogate mom fights to save baby she is carrying as biological parents push for ABORTION over treatable heart condition

A SURROGATE mom is fighting to save the unborn boy she is carrying after his biological parents demanded that she abort him over a severe heart defect.

McKenna West refused to end the pregnancy after learning that a series of operations could give the baby a chance at life.



The Alaska nurse, who is now in Texas, has become locked in a bitter court battle with the California couple as her September 2 due date rapidly approaches.

West was 20 weeks pregnant when an ultrasound revealed there was no blood flowing through the left side of the baby’s heart.



She said the devastating diagnosis came without warning after earlier scans and genetic tests had appeared normal.

“It was completely unexpected,” West told Live Action.



A maternal-fetal medicine specialist diagnosed the boy with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, known as HLHS.

The rare congenital defect leaves the left side of the heart too underdeveloped to properly pump blood around the body.

Babies with HLHS require urgent treatment after birth and will usually undergo three major operations.

The first, known as the Norwood procedure, is normally performed within days of delivery.



It is followed by the Glenn procedure at around four to six months and the Fontan operation at roughly two or three years old.

NewYork-Presbyterian says around 72 percent of children receiving surgical treatment survive to age five.

Among those who reach five, approximately 90 percent survive to 18, although patients require lifelong heart care and may later need further procedures or a transplant.

Court documents reportedly describe the baby, whom West calls Gabriel, as a standard-risk patient whose condition may be an isolated heart defect.

West’s doctor said the boy appeared to face a low risk of dying during the first operation, according to filings obtained by Live Action.



But West said the biological parents, identified only as A.B. and C.D., raised the possibility of abortion immediately after the diagnosis.

“I knew that I didn’t want to have to go through it,” she told the outlet.

West had become their surrogate through Connecticut-based Worldwide Surrogacy Specialists after meeting the couple over Zoom.

“It felt like a perfect match,” she recalled.

West said the surrogacy agreement contained a clause requiring her to terminate the pregnancy if an “anomaly” was discovered.



She had questioned the clause before signing, but said the agency assured her that such circumstances were rare.

After the diagnosis, West asked whether financial help could be arranged to cover the baby’s expected medical costs.

She also shared accounts of people living with HLHS in an effort to persuade the couple to continue the pregnancy.

But West said her fears grew after one of the parents told her they had removed the baby’s earlier ultrasound picture from their refrigerator.

He reportedly said she could mail them the latest scan but should address the envelope only to him.



West began researching specialist hospitals and found a pediatric center in Dallas that treats babies with the condition.

Children’s Health says all newborns who underwent the Norwood operation at its center in 2020 and 2021 survived, compared with a national survival rate of 85 percent at the time.

West offered to stay with a friend in Texas to reduce the couple’s travel and accommodation costs.

However, a liaison from the surrogacy agency reportedly told her the parents remained concerned about the boy’s future quality of life.

Days after the diagnosis, West was informed that they had formally requested an abortion.



The procedure was initially scheduled in Seattle for April 28 and 29, when she would have been 23 weeks pregnant.

It was later moved to May 6 and 7, when West would have been 24 weeks along, after she struggled to arrange for someone to accompany her.

In court papers, West described feeling horrified by the prospect of undergoing the procedure and said she feared how she would live with the decision afterward.

She also worried that refusing would expose her and her two young children to financial ruin.

West said the turning point came when her brother offered to adopt the baby with his wife.



“We’ll adopt this baby,” he told her, according to West.

The nurse then contacted her friend, podcaster Ellen Fisher, who connected her with anti-abortion campaigner Lila Rose.

West said Rose offered to help move her family to Texas and connect her with lawyers and doctors.

“I finally felt hopeful,” West told Live Action.

The biological parents have since sought $250,000 from West, including money already paid under the agreement and additional alleged damages.



They are also pursuing legal recognition of their parental rights in California, despite language in the contract stating that Alaska law would govern the agreement.

The couple wants West to give birth in California under the care of a medical team selected there.

West’s attorneys claim the parents have not committed to approving the operations after the boy is delivered and may instead choose comfort care.

West has said she will travel to California and surrender any custody claim if the couple guarantees that the baby will receive surgery.

She has otherwise asked an Alaska court to award her sole custody so doctors in Texas can treat him.



“I want to fight for him because he deserves that chance,” West said.

She added that there was no guarantee the treatment would work but insisted the boy deserved the opportunity to live outside the womb.

On July 28, the Alaska Superior Court rejected an effort to immediately force West to move to California.

However, it ruled that a California court could decide where she delivers and which medical team treats her.

The State of Alaska intervened by arguing that its constitution protects a surrogate’s power to make her own pregnancy and medical decisions.



“The constitutional right of privacy protects a woman’s autonomy,” the state said in its filing.

The biological parents objected and accused West and her attorneys of using the state to ignore their parental and privacy rights.

They argued that West was causing “confusion and stress” when the child’s interests should be the only consideration.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A California court has granted the couple a judgment recognizing their parental rights.

West is now challenging that decision through an emergency appeal as the fight over the baby’s birthplace and medical treatment continues.

News.title: World’s third smallest country changes its name – and may even need to relocate entirely
News.content:
SMALL CHANGE World’s third smallest country changes its name – and may even need to relocate entirely

THE world’s third-smallest country has changed its name – and could be forced to abandon its homeland altogether.

The Pacific island nation of Nauru will now officially be known as the Republic of Naoero, President David Adeang has announced.



The country’s international code will also change from NRU to NRO, while its citizens will be known as dei-Naoero instead of Nauruans.

The move restores the island’s traditional name, according to a government statement.



Officials said the nation became internationally known as Nauru because its indigenous name was difficult for foreign visitors to pronounce.

“The proposed change seeks to more faithfully honour our nation’s heritage, our language, and our identity,” the President said.

The legislation has already passed two rounds of voting, with lawmakers deciding a public referendum won’t be necessary.

A statement said: “While a referendum is intended to determine the will of the people, the name Naoero has never been lost, but rather waiting to be fully embraced.



“The designation is already the identity of the people, is on the national coat of arms, and spoken in the community; and importantly is allowed by the Constitution.”

The government said it is already working with foreign governments to ensure the new name is formally recognised.

Australia and New Zealand’s foreign ministries, along with the US and Chinese embassies in the region, have already begun referring to the country as Naoero on their websites.

The decision is the latest example of a nation shedding a colonial-era identity.

In 2018, the African kingdom of Eswatini reverted to its historic name after decades of being known as Swaziland.



Other countries have opted for similar changes as part of a national rebrand, including Türkiye, which asked the United Nations in 2022 to adopt the Turkish spelling.

Home to around 12,000 people, Naoero is the world’s third-smallest country by population, behind Tuvalu and Vatican City.

The remote coral atoll was colonised by Germany before later being administered by Australia.

After gaining independence in 1968, the island has endured repeated hardship.

Vast phosphate deposits made it extremely wealthy during the 1970s, but the boom ended when the industry collapsed.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Today, Naoero faces a different threat as rising sea levels put its future at risk.

The danger has prompted the government to try and attract overseas investment to fund the relocation of people and critical infrastructure to higher ground.

News.title: Shocking moment saucy shoppers get intimate on IKEA display bed in full view of stunned customers and families
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment two randy IKEA shoppers begin heavy petting on a display bed in full view of other customers.

The frisky couple were captured kissing and caressing each other on top of the covers in a blush-inducing video.



Confronting footage shows the couple appearing completely lost in their own world as they explore each other’s bodies.

The public display of affection took place in full view of shocked families in an IKEA showroom in Taiwan.



An outraged mum filmed the public tryst and shared the clip on social media, days after she captured the steamy scene on 16.uly.

She said her child spotted the couple and told her the display was “disgusting”.

The mum posted the clip on platform Threads and blasted the pair for being unable to control their sexual impulses.

“Go home, get in the car, or rent a room,” she wrote.



Other social media users were also outraged, with one writing: “IKEA is not a hotel”.

Some suggested IKEA should put up signs banning any canoodling.

The pair were both wearing black T-shirts and had dumped their shoes on the bed next to them.

The woman wore a low- cut top with an exposed waist.

Under Taiwan’s public indecency laws, the couple could face up to a year in prison or a fine of about £220.



IKEA had to crack down on sexual behaviour in its stores before, when a Chinese porn star filmed a graphic video of herself performing a sex act in 2020.

The 16-minute-long X-rated video was shared widely online and prompted IKEA to condemn the behaviour and ramp up security measures.

The video is believed to have been filmed in Guangzhou, and similarly took place in the bed display area.

The woman at the centre of the risqué film, reported at the time to be a porn star called Fullfive, and her camera operator faced criminal charges and a three- year prison term.

News.title: Gorgeous English beach loved by the late Queen is forced to CLOSE due to ‘raw sewage spill’
News.content:
A FAMOUS English beach has been closed following a sewage spill.

The popular site was known for having links to the Royal Family, including the late Queen Elizabeth II and Princess Margaret.

St Mawes harbour, in Cornwall, has been forced to close after raw sewage was dumped into its waters for up to five hours on Monday (August 3).



As a result, the St Mawes Pier and Harbour Company have advised visitors to avoid direct contact with the seawater for “a minimum of 48 hours” after the spill had stopped.



The leak was the result of a burst pipe on Sunday evening, which South West Water has said it is currently working on repairing and “are tankering to reduce impact to the local environment”.

The Environment Agency told The Telegraph: “Officers are busy responding to a sewage spill in St Mawes, Cornwall.

“Sewage is being taken away by tanker while South West Water repair a pipe which burst on Sunday evening.



“We would advise against going into the water for recreation as sewage is still present in the harbour area.”

The agency confirmed that no further discharges had taken place but daily water quality sampling would continue, in order to ensure visitors and residents would remain safe.

However, this is not the only sewage spill to take place across the UK over the past few days.

Elsewhere, swimmers were urged not to bathe at Polstreath Beach, due to the presence of sewage pollution.



South West Water said they were currently investigating the source of the spill, as the Environment Agency maintained it would “continue to monitor the situation”.

This comes as water companies exceeded sewage discharge limits at 65 bathing sites since May 15.

Jo Morley, the head of campaigns at Surfers Against Sewage, said: “It’s the same classic water company behaviour – years of prioritising payouts over pipes, whilst we risk swimming in sewage.”

Known as the Saint Tropez of England, the sheltered harbour of St Mawes often attracts high-profile holidaymakers including Queen Elizabeth II, the Prince and Princess of Wales and Kate Winslet.

News.title: Scratch card winner scoops £272k jackpot - but his day gets even better
News.content:
Scratch card winner scoops £272k jackpot - but his day gets even better

One lucky winner pocketed an impressive £272,000 scratch card lottery jackpot, but things got even better hours later on the "Millionaire Blowout" game in Ohio, USA

View 3 Images An American man has won a whopping $366,000 on a scratch card (stock) (Image: Getty Images/Tetra images RF)

Winning a cash prize is a dream for many, but the chances of landing a top lottery jackpot - whether it’s Powerball or even a scratch card - can feel like a long shot. Yet some people seem to have luck on their side. In rare cases, it even strikes twice in a single day.

‌



This was the case for one extraordinarily fortunate man from the States, who raked in about £272k on a scratch card one day - only to land a further £13.6k on a second card (after tax).

‌



Unnamed, the enigmatic Ohio player opted for a massive lump sum when he scored on the "Millionaire Blowout" game. His grand total was nearly 286k, and it seems he has big plans for the cash.

‌



As many prospective winners might wish, he's treating himself to an extended holiday and a motor, although he says he'll also hand over some to his kids and top up his nest egg.

View 3 Images He walked away with an eye-watering $366,250 (stock) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

At just 21, Iowa resident Timothy Schultz hit the jackpot, winning $28 million. But years later, he says the experience taught him hard lessons — and he has a few cautionary words he would share with his younger self.

‌



He stated: "I'd probably start by saying, 'Buckle up'. That dream of winning is about to become reality, and your life is going to change faster than you can possibly imagine."

Following his win, Timothy said he was sent "stacks of letters from strangers asking for help", as reported by UNILAD. He continued: "Lending money could quickly complicate even a close friendship."

Speaking to Fox News about the matter, he said: "Most people were supportive and happy for me, but I did receive stacks of letters from people asking for money."

‌



He also explained that some saw him as a "walking, talking ATM machine".

View 3 Images On the lucky winner's agenda is an extended vacation and new car (stock) (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Powerball’s jackpots have reached eye-watering levels in recent years. Just three years ago, the top prize soared to a record $2.04 billion — the biggest Powerball jackpot ever — and was claimed by Edwin Castro.

Article continues below

More recently, an Arkansas-bought ticket landed an approximate £1.3 billion win, which was billed at the time as one of the largest lottery payouts in US history.

The odds of matching all the numbers were still the same long shot: roughly one in 292.2 million. It was also only the second time Arkansas had produced a Powerball jackpot winner.

The game has now crossed the Atlantic to the UK, where the latest jackpot has climbed past £372.4 million. Any winner would receive the money as an annuity, paid in 30 yearly instalments — more than £12 million each year.

News.title: Father and daughter swept to their deaths in Fistral Beach tragedy as he tried to save her
News.content:
Father and daughter swept to their deaths in Fistral Beach tragedy as he tried to save her

John Peter Collins, 66, and his daughter Samantha Adele Collins, 32, from Doncaster, drowned at Fistral Beach in Newquay on July 26, an inquest opening has heard

View 2 Images The tragic deaths happened at Fistral Beach (Image: William Dax / SWNS)

A father and his daughter were swept to their deaths at one of the UK's best-known surfing beaches after he entered the sea in a desperate attempt to rescue her, an inquest opening has heard.

‌



John Peter Collins, 66, and his daughter Samantha Adele Collins, 32, were pulled from the water at Fistral Beach in Newquay on July 26.

‌



On Tuesday, Cornwall Coroner's Court heard their family, from Doncaster, South Yorkshire, had been on holiday in the seaside town.

‌



Assistant coroner Emma Hillson said: "Samantha Collins was on holiday with her family in Newquay. She and her father were fishing on rocks when Samantha was dragged into the sea. John tried to save her, but very sadly was unable to so and they both lost their lives."

View 2 Images Fistral Beach in Newquay, Cornwall (file image) (Image: William Dax / SWNS)

Adele Collins, the wife of Mr Collins and mother of Ms Collins, identified their bodies, the hearing was told.

‌



Post-mortem examinations were performed at the Royal Cornwall Hospital in Treliske on July 29. The provisional cause of death for both father and daughter was given as drowning.

"Given the reported circumstances of the death and the provisional cause of death, I have reason to suspect the death may be as a result of an unnatural cause," the coroner said.

"I am going to adjourn for a provisional full hearing date of July 19, 2027, at 10am, with a time estimate of three hours. This will be a joint inquest."

‌



The hearing in Truro heard Mr Collins was married and a retired technical engineer, while his daughter was single.

Devon and Cornwall Police previously confirmed officers were called to Fistral Beach at about 9.45pm on July 26. Both Mr Collins and his daughter had been recovered from the water. Emergency services attended, but the pair were pronounced dead at the scene.

Ms Collins is believed to have entered the water carrying a handbag, described as orange or peach in colour, with a shoulder strap.

Article continues below

A police spokesperson previously said it was "thought to contain a number of personal items of great sentimental value to her loved ones".

"At what is an incredibly difficult time for the family, they would take great comfort in being reunited with these belongings if possible," she said.

Anyone who finds a bag matching the description is asked to hand it into Newquay police station, or to contact police, quoting the incident number 50260197209.

News.title: Tragedy as Brit mum-of-three dead after becoming trapped in raging Spain wildfires
News.content:
Tragedy as Brit mum-of-three dead after becoming trapped in raging Spain wildfires

Lisa Fryett and her partner Simon Batchelor, both from Essex, were hospitalised with life-threatening injuries after becoming caught in a devastating Spanish wildfire last month.

View Image Simon Batchelor and Lisa Fryett. (Image: Jam Press/GoFundMe)

A British woman has died in Spain just weeks after a devastating wildfire left her and her partner in critical condition.

‌



Lisa Fryett and Simon Batchelor, both from Essex, were staying near Bédar and Los Gallardos in Spain when the blaze broke out in nearby villages.

‌



The couple were rescued from the fire and rushed to the hospital with life-threatening injuries following the blaze on July 14, with a GoFundMe update from a page set up to support the family confirming that Lisa has since passed away, surrounded by her family in Spain.

‌



"Our hearts are completely broken, and there are simply no words to describe the pain we are feeling," a post on the fundraiser read.

"Lisa fought so incredibly hard, and we are so grateful that her loved ones were able to be by her side, surrounding her with love until the very end.

‌



"We would like to thank every single person who has donated, shared our fundraiser, or kept our family in your thoughts and prayers. The love, kindness and generosity we have received have brought us comfort during the most devastating time of our lives."

They added: "Thanks to your incredible support, our family has been able to remain together in Spain, allowing us to be by Lisa’s side when she needed us most. That is something we will be forever grateful for."

More than £650,000 has been raised so far to help support the family and "give Lisa the beautiful send off she deserves."

Article continues below

Mr Batchelor is still hospitalised in critical condition, with the fundraiser asking people to "Please continue to keep Simon in your thoughts and prayers as he remains in critical condition. Our family is holding onto hope and taking each day as it comes, and your continued love, support and prayers mean the world to us."

A spokesperson from the British Foreign Office said: "We are supporting the family of a British woman who has died in Spain and are in contact with the local authorities."

News.title: How Andy Burnham could raise huge amount with tax raid on banks and oil giants
News.content:
How Andy Burnham could raise huge amount with tax raid on banks and oil giants

HSBC and BP have become the latest industry giants to announce profit bonanzas, helped by the Middle East conflict, while ordinary households are left reeling by the financial fall-out. It has prompted new calls for the companies to pay more to offset the impact - but what are chances?

View 5 Images Andy Burnham has refused to be drawn on North Sea oil after pressure from US President Donald Trump (Image: Temilade Adelaja/Reuters Pool vi)

Big banks and energy giants have announced another wave of eye-watering profits over the past week, fuelled by the ongoing Middle East war.

‌



And as companies coin it in - what one critic dubbed a “war bonus” - ordinary households are paying the price through higher prices for everything from energy and fuel to food in the supermarket.

‌



It is why there are fresh calls for new PM Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey to take action against the firms, especially in the case of banks in the form of a windfall tax.

‌



The criticism of energy giants also comes against the backdrop of the extreme weather, with drought conditions across the UK and Europe, and devastating wildfire. Critics have linked the current situation with the impact of fossil fuel firms on man-made climate change.

View 5 Images Chancellor John Healey and PM Andy Burnham are likely to face growing questions in the coming months about a possible windfall tax on banks

Just how much money are these companies making?

In short, huge amounts at the moment. While it’s true that banks and energy firms’ earnings can go through cycles, for different reasons, both sectors have enjoyed bumper profits for some time.

‌



Britain’s often called ‘big four’ banks - HSBC, Lloyds Banking Group, NatWest and Barclays - have netted more than £29billion profit between them in the past six months.

BP, meanwhile, booked a £6.6billion profit for the same period, having well over doubled from the first half of last year.

View 5 Images While oil producers have seen profits surge, motorists have endured pain at the pumps (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

‌



Why are they making so much money?

In the case of energy producers, it is thanks in part to a surge in wholesale oil and gas prices after the outbreak of the US-Israel war with Iran at the end of February.

While the conflict meant added costs to producers in the region too, the price jump ensured they got that much more for what they produce.

There is a cut across when it comes to banks, as the energy shock caused by the price spikes have driven inflation back up, or at least slowed an expected fall.

‌



Higher for longer inflation means central banks, including the Bank of England, have delayed possible interest rate cuts, and have even considered increases. The longer rates say high, the better it is for lenders.

View 5 Images North Sea oil and gas producers are likely to argue they are already heavily taxed ahead of the autumn Budget (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

How much are banks and oil firms taxed?

Oil producers argue they’re heavily taxed already, at 78%. That’s made up of a higher rate of corporation tax, an energy profits levy and a supplementary charge.

‌



According to trade body UK Finance, banks operating here pay a total tax rate of 46.6%, though that includes things like employers’ national insurance. That compared to 42.2% in Amsterdam, 38.9% in Frankfurt, 28.9% in Dublin, and 27.9% in New York. It estimates the sector paid £43.3 billion in taxes for the financial year to the end of March 2025.

View 5 Images HSBC, the big money sponsor of the The Queen's Club tennis championship in June, has seen profits jump this year (Image: Getty Images for LTA)

What could the government do?

One option being pushed by campaigners and the TUC is a new windfall tax on banks.

‌



It is based on the idea of a levy imposed on companies that have benefited from something they were not responsible for, in this case the Middle East conflict.

The Tories have introduced windfall taxes various times in the past. Indeed, Margaret Thatcher’s Chancellor, Geoffrey Howe, announced a 2.5% levy on banks in 1981, with a special tax on North Sea producers following the next year. Gordon Brown, when Labour Chancellor, upped a supplementary charge on North Sea producers to 20% in 2006, and Tory Chancellor George Osborne hiked it further in 2011.

The TUC and others are focusing on a surcharge on top of what corporation tax banks pay. It is currently a 3% add-on, having been cut from 8% by the Tories in 2023.

‌



They claim restoring it to 8% could raise £9billion over four years, doubling it to 16% would rake in £24billion. An upper end hike to 35% could collect £60billion over four years, they say.

How likely are tax hikes on banks and energy producers?

It’s too early to know ahead of the autumn Budget in late October, but a windfall tax on banks is a possible “low hanging fruit” for Chancellor John Healey. Expect heavy lobbying from the sector between now and then, as it argues higher taxes will only mean less money for lending, with the knock on impact for the economy.

Nigel Green ,of advisory firm deVere Group, said: “Every time a government talks about taxing banks harder, people assume it only hits shareholders in the City.

Article continues below

“It never stays there. Banks pass costs on, and the people who end up paying are ordinary customers with a mortgage, a savings account, or a current card.”

Higher taxes on North Sea producers could prove a short-term money spinner. The Treasury collected £4.5billion from UK oil and gas production in the 2024/25 financial year, though that was down from £6.1 billion in 2023/24. However, a hike doesn’t look likely at this stage, especially given the scale of job losses in the sector. If anything, Burnham and Healey are facing calls to ease pressure on producers and allow some form of new drilling. Oil firms also point out that the bulk of their profits are made abroad, so any tax hike here may not deliver a hoped-for tax surge.

News.title: 'Our little Maya, two, was murdered — we'll suffer more pain with the early release scheme'
News.content:
'Our little Maya, two, was murdered — we'll suffer more pain with the early release scheme'

EXCLUSIVE: The family of murdered Maya Chappell, of Shotton Colliery, County Durham, say restrictions on the type of offenders who could be released early from jail "don't go far enough"

View 5 Images Maya Chappell was killed in 2022 (Image: gofundme.com)

A mum who allowed her partner to murder her toddler could be eligible for early release from prison.

‌



But Maya Chappell's family has hit out at the move, arguing it will leave them suffering more pain. Dana Carr was jailed for nine years for child cruelty and allowing the death of her daughter Maya, two, who was shaken to death by Carr's partner Michael Daymond. Daymond was jailed for life following the senseless attack.

‌



But Carr could now be up for early release as part of the government's controversial scheme. Maya's great-aunt Gemma Chappell told the Mirror this move "completely takes victims right back".

‌



Around 5,000 people are expected to be released early under sentencing changes part of the scheme to tackle overcrowding in jails. This is down from 6,000 after the government announced that rapists and child sex offenders would be exempt from early release, after a review of the policy was ordered by Andy Burnham shortly after he became Prime Minister.

Andy Burnham backs Mirror water safety campaign as drownings spike in hot weather READ MORE :

View 5 Images Maya's family have hit out at the early release scheme (Image: Gemma Chappell)

Gemma said her sister received an email from Prison Services around three weeks ago which said the early releases could potentially impact their family and Carr's early release. The great-aunt said: "I didn't think it was going to affect us because I thought surely they'll not let such a serious offence cause doubt and I was so wrong."

‌



Carr had left Maya in Daymond's sole care on September 28, 2022, before the girl collapsed when he fiercely shook her. The partner - who had been with Carr for just nine weeks - had learned his Universal Credit had been stopped before he attacked the little girl, in County Durham. She died in hospital two days later as a result of a "constellation" of injuries, having never regained consciousness, a court heard.

Daymond was found guilty of murdering Maya and was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum of 20 years. He was never eligible for release under the sentencing act.

View 5 Images Gemma Chappell, pictured with Maya, has spoken to the Mirror

‌



Great-aunt Gemma said she welcomed the move to block rapists and child sex offenders but was furious at the potential release of Carr and said "they shouldn't stop there". Gemma told the Mirror: "They should continue to be under review about offenses that are committed that are serious. And there's still victims and families out there who face this reality that the person responsible, such as Dana Carr, who was who was charged with causing and allowing the death of a child and child neglect."

Gemma revealed the decision has impacted Maya's dad James and said: "She [Carr] knew it was going on, but did nothing to protect Maya, because she was so obsessed about this guy, and she's going to be released. I mean, that's unimaginable. And the harm that that's going to cause to our family, to James... it's ridiculous that that's going to happen."

Carr lost an appeal to reduce her sentence, in 2025, as judges said the original sentence was "severe, but was not wrong in principle or manifestly excessive". Gemma said before the appeal her family had asked for Carr's sentence to be extended.

‌



On this, Gemma told the Mirror: "It just completely takes victims right back, it takes James back, it takes us back. We've not been heard. It was great that we got that answer when she went to that High Court. That gave us some alleviation, and we realised then that we can try and get through our trauma knowing that she's going to serve at least nine years."

She added : "That's coming at the cost and the safety of the public and at victims. And, victims voices are not being heard... It just hasn't gone far enough - they haven't listened to other victims with regards to this."

5 View 5 Images Dana Carr could be released early (Image: PA) 5 View 5 Images Michael Daymond was jailed for life for murder (Image: PA)

‌



Justice Secretary Alex Norris, this morning on BBC Radio 4, said the government was directly engaging with families of victims but Gemma claimed this has not happened with her family.

She continued: "I've just heard the justice secretary saying 'we've been speaking to victims', no you haven't because you haven't spoken to us. You haven't asked us, what you've done is you've told us." Gemma said her sister received a call from the government yesterday to again inform them that Carr was eligible for early release.

The great-aunt said: "There's still victims of families out there who face this reality that the person responsible, such as Dana Carr... and she's going to be released. That's unimaginable and the harm that's going to cause, it's just ridiculous that that's going to happen."

Article continues below

Gemma also called on the government to carry on looking into the release scheme and said: "I think they should still be reviewing this. How can they review it within a week? That's ridiculous."

The two-year-old's family has been fighting for the government to pass Maya's Law, which would involve sharing information to a parent or guardian where a child is at risk due to a parent or caregiver's known history. Gemma said the release scheme "strengthens Maya's Law" to "protect and put that preventive measure for these vulnerable children".

The Mirror has reached out to the Ministry of Justice for comment.

News.title: Horror as woman found dead in Liverpool hotel and police make 'murder' arrests
News.content:
Horror as woman found dead in Liverpool hotel and police make 'murder' arrests

Tributes have poured in for Suzanne Menagh, who died at the White Star Line Hotel on James Street, Liverpool city centre, as pals say she had 'heart of gold'

View 2 Images Multiple tributes have been paid after Suzanne Menagh's death (Image: Facebook)

A "lovely" woman who died at a hotel in Liverpool city centre has been named and pictured as police arrested two on suspicion of murder.

Suzanne Menagh, who was 40 years old, became unwell at the White Star Line Hotel on James Street but, despite the paramedics' best efforts, she was pronounced dead at the scene. Merseyside Police are treating the death as unexplained and two people have been arrested on suspicion of murder.

A post-mortem examination has been carried out to establish Ms Menagh's cause of death but the results are withheld pending toxicology reports. Meanwhile, tributes have started pouring in for Ms Menagh, who pals say had "a heart of gold".

Ry's Competitions, based in Bootle, Merseyside, described Suzanne as a "valued and loyal member" of its community. In a tribute, the company said: "From everyone at Ry's Competitions, we would like to offer our heartfelt condolences to the Menagh family following the sad loss of Suzanne.

"She was always a pleasure to have as part of our community. Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with Melissa, the entire Menagh family, and all those who knew and loved Suzanne during this incredibly difficult time. Rest in peace, Suzanne."

View 2 Images Police outside the White Star Line Hotel on James Street (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Many others also shared messages in Suzanne's memory, Liverpool ECHO reports. Darhyl Sharp wrote: "She had a heart of gold. Still can't get my head around it. RIP Sue, you will be missed."

Amme Snobbig said: "Lovely girl. She's going to be missed by so many. R.I.P Sue." Leanne Kelly posted: "I can't believe you have gone, not going to see you again. Thinking of your mum, dad and sisters at this sad time."

Kenny Fields wrote: "Thinking of all the Menagh family at this very sad time. Rest in peace, Suzanne. Gone far too soon. You will be sadly missed." Olivia Lomas said: "Rest in peace Suzanne. The world is a cruel place." Amy Benson added: "Absolutely devastating news. Fly high angel."

Honey Blossom Pomfret also paid tribute, writing: "Someone I worked with has sadly passed away. I haven't spoken for a while with her but got on with her. She was a really lovely woman. RIP Suzanne Menagh. My prayers go out to your family and loved ones."

Merseyside Police confirmed a 47-year-old man from Kirkby, Merseyside, and a 34-year-old woman from Liverpool have been arrested on suspicion of murder. A 31-year-old man from Liverpool has also been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

All three have been conditionally bailed while enquiries are ongoing. Two police forensic vans were seen outside The White Star Line Hotel yesterday evening (August 3) as officers continued their investigation.

Article continues below

A spokesperson for The White Star Line Hotel said: "Our thoughts are with the family and loved ones of the deceased at this time. We are assisting the police in their enquiries in any way we can."

News.title: Su Pollard reveals final phone call before co-star's tragic death and why her marriage really ended
News.content:
Hi-de-Hi! star Su Pollard first realised she was famous when her name was the answer to a crossword clue. The actress, who played chalet maid Peggy Ollerenshaw in the BBC1 comedy set in the fictional Maplins Holiday Camp in 1950s Essex, says: “I saw the crossword, and did a double take. It read, ‘what was the name of the actress that played Peggy in Hi-de-Hi!?’ And I couldn’t believe it. ‘It’s me, it’s me’!”

Now 76, Su has particularly fond memories of acting alongside Ruth Madoc, who played Gladys, a yellowcoat (the hosts and performers) in the series that ran from 1980-1988. She was devastated when Ruth died on December 9, 2022, aged 79, following surgery after a fall she suffered earlier that week.

Marilyn Monroe’s legendary photographer opens up on their extraordinary bond READ MORE :

She says of their time on Hi-de-Hi! which at its peak pulled in more than 20 million viewers: “There was no envy between us. None of this, ‘you’ve got more lines than I should have.’ We worked together as a really good team.”

View 7 Images 1980 - Su Pollard as Peggy Ollerenshaw in the BBC sitcom Hi-de-Hi! (Image: ©BBC)

‌



Reflecting on Ruth’s death, she continues: “I’m so glad that the day before she had the operation, I rang her and just said, ‘good luck, babe. Hope it goes well and let me know how you get on.’

“Well, you can imagine the shock here when I was told that she’d passed away. It was awful. I think of her all the time. When you’ve worked with people for a long time, they’re not just colleagues. You see their kids grow up, how well they’re doing. We were fortunate to have had that kind of wonderful, extra joy of familial comfort with each other. She liked her whisky and a fag. And, you know, she was a great opera singer.”

Su, who got to number 2 in the UK Singles Chart in 1986 with Starting Together, went on to star in BBC1’s You Rang, M’Lord, as well as appearing in West End Musicals and doing 46 pantos over the years. She says: “Pantomimes are pure, unadulterated fun. Joy. The audience is given permission to have a good time. People still yell Hi-di-Hi! at me on stage!”

View 7 Images Actress Ruth Madoc, who played yellowcoat Gladys Pugh, died aged 79 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But her favourite part ever was not Peggy, but rather Miss Hannigan, the evil orphanage matron in Annie. She says: “I did it for 10 years off and on - 12 week tours at a time. Add all those tours up and I've been Miss Hannigan for two and a half years straight. She became a part of me.

“I always found something different. She’s brilliant. You could really play with her. I tried to make her as real as possible. I hardly wore any makeup, she wore this terrible blue eye shadow, it was up my nose and round my eyes. I could get ready in five minutes. I'd throw my wig across the dressing room and stand on it to make it look like she hadn't had her hair done in five years.”

And she prefers playing a baddie. She says: “There’s no competition, especially in a panto. I’d rather get down and dirty with a baddie than play someone squeaky clean.”

However, this Christmas, she’s set to play “a good fairy in bovva boots” in Sleeping Beauty at the Crewe Lyceum Theatre. Despite her diverse career, the actress - whose book Su Pollard: Fully Charged is out on August 13 - will always be remembered for Hi-de-Hi!

‌



View 7 Images Su Pollard’s parents, Don and Hilda (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

She recalls one hilarious encounter when she was recognised by the lead singer of Queen. She says: “I clearly remember meeting Freddie Mercury on the dancefloor of the Copacabana Club in Earls Court, mid-80s. This man came up to me and said, very politely, ‘Do you mind if I join you?’ I nearly screamed out loud. He was completely relaxed and charming.

"He told me how much he loved Hi-de-Hi! and then, to my delight, asked me to say ‘Hi-de-Hi!’, one of the famous catchphrases from the show, properly for him. I obliged loudly, of course, and he immediately replied ‘Ho-de-Ho!’ Then he asked me for a picture.”

Sue has also been heckled by a Beatle. She says: “When I came off stage at the Royal Variety Performance I found myself standing next to Paul McCartney and his wife Linda. Suddenly he piped up, ‘Hi-de-Hi!’. He told me how much his mum loved the show and asked if I would sign an autograph for her!”.

‌



View 7 Images Su Pollard, who was undone by a sandwich on Celebrity Masterchef (Image: BBC/Shine TV)

She also tap danced with Princess Diana at 10 Downing Street, when they were both at a charity event. She says of Princess Di: “She told me she loved my dress, saying ‘it’s like a rainbow’. It had been knitted by a fan - squares of wool, in a patchwork.

“She said, ‘I hear you’re doing Me and My Girl . I said, ‘Yes, but I’m struggling with the tapping.’ She told me she’d learned ballet when she was younger, but had recently been learning tap dancing herself and found it difficult to master.

“I showed her a couple of steps, and she said, ‘let’s do something together then!’ So we did! It was really fabulous, just off the cuff and great, it was terrific! She was really generous of spirit.”

‌



Growing up in Nottingham, Su has an early memory of singing a song at Christmas for her parents Hilda and Don, who worked for Players, the cigarette makers, when she was four. Su says: “Another career path never entered my mind. I was born wanting to perform. They always encouraged me. One of my earliest memories is my mum singing along to the radio, so I always think of her when I do radio.”

View 7 Images Su Pollard as the Wicked Queen in Snow White (Image: www.eggshell-blue.co.uk / DRIK)

Still a regular guest on the BBC Radio 4 panel game Just a Minute, she adds: “I get my work ethic from my dad, who took approximately two weeks off in his life.”

After cutting her teeth in local theatre, Su’s first appearance on national TV came in 1975, on talent show Opportunity Knocks. And her first foray into sitcoms was in 1979’s Two Up, Two Down, before Hi-de-Hi! came along in 1980.

‌



And, despite six decades in showbiz, she has no plans to retire and hopes to take her one-woman show, Su Pollard: Still Fully Charged, to New Zealand soon, having toured the UK for the past two years. “Don’t mention the ‘r’ word! It’s not something I’m even considering - I’m having far too much fun,” she says of retiring.

Happily single, Su was previously married to author Peter Keogh from 1984 to 1992 - who was publicly outed as gay soon after their honeymoon, thanks to a highly publicised court trial in which he was acquitted of theft. She says: “I’m great mates with my ex-husband's husband.”

View 7 Images Su Pollard: Fully Charged (Mirror Books, £22) is on sale August 13th. Pre-order on Amazon now

Charming and self-deprecating, Su, is a champion of fellow comedy actresses. She says: “I’ve been watching Ann Droid with Sue Johnson. It’s brilliant - I hope they make more.”

‌



Her advice to comedy writers is simple. She says: “As long as your dialogue is witty and it’s got heart,you’re on to a winner. That was the formula for the sitcom phenomenon of the 1950s, then the 1980s - and it’s the same today. That’s what people want.”

Meanwhile, the best advice she ever received was from director Tudor Davies. She says: “I was 25. He said, ‘don’t be up yourself, Pollard’. I’m pleased to say I’ve stuck to that ever since.”

*Su Pollard: Fully Charged (Mirror Books, £22) is on sale August 13th. Pre-order on Amazon now.

News.title: Should Andy Burnham introduce a windfall tax to ease cost of living? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Should Andy Burnham introduce a windfall tax to ease cost of living? Take our poll and have your say

After the 'big four' banks made more than £29 billion combined in the space of six months, The Mirror is asking if Andy Burnham should consider a windfall tax to help struggling Brits

View 2 Images Andy Burnham said he wanted to tackle the cost of living crisis (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

Andy Burnham has signalled he will tackle the cost of living crisis facing Brits with The Mirror asking whether the Prime Minister should consider a windfall tax to help those who are struggling.

‌



The new Prime Minister previously told The Sunday Mirror helping hard-pressed households was his top priority and revealed he wanted to do more to bring down utility bills and fail fares. Burnham has slotted home several quick wins since entering No10 Downing Street two weeks ago, including a month of free bus travel for under-16s and beginning a national conversation into the state of adult social care.

‌



But the cost of living remains a top concern among Brits with the economy being the top issue for UK adults, according to YouGov. Burnham used his first days to announce VAT will be slashed from electricity bills from October, bus fares will be capped at £2 and pubs, social clubs and live music venues will get a 20 per cent cut to business rates from April.

‌



View 2 Images HSBC's profits have been boosted by a widening gap between what it pays savers and makes from lending (Image: Lucy North/PA)

Andy Burnham urged to unleash tax raid on banks amid £55billion profit bonanza READ MORE :

Oil giant BP's profits more than DOUBLE while households suffer rising energy bill costs pain READ MORE :

But The Mirror is asking whether the Prime Minister should consider a windfall tax raid to help Brits make their money go further. The Trade Union Congress (TUC) has called for a windfall tax on banks to help bring down energy bills for millions of households.

‌



HSBC fuelled the plea for the new PM and Chancellor John Healey to target lenders in the Autumn Budget after it announced half year profits surged by almost a quarter to £14.5 billion. It comes after a bumper round of results from rivals Lloyds Banking Group, Barclays and NatWest. boosted by higher for longer interest rates.

The 'big four' have together made more than £29 billion in the space of just six months. The TUC has now asked the government to use the money to pay for a social tariff that, it claims would bring down energy bills by up to £559 a year for those on low and middle incomes.

Article continues below

TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak said: “There is now a mountain of evidence to suggest that banks can easily afford to pay more tax. While higher interest rates have meant mortgage misery and bigger bills for the rest of us, the big banks have been rolling in it.

“Andy Burnham has rightly prioritised cost of living measures in his first days as prime minister, but as the war in Iran rumbles on energy prices will rise further - and the government will need to do more to protect households. That’s why it’s time to increase the tax on bank profits to cut bills. It’s common sense and it’s the right thing to do.”

The four big banks combined are estimated at this stage to make £55.3billion profit for the whole year, up sharply from 2025, and equivalent to around £1,750 every second.

News.title: Video shows Russian drone chasing Ukrainian street vendor in 'human safari' attack
News.content:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has shared a video on social media of a drone hunting down a man in southern Ukraine, saying it showed an instance of a Russian "safari" attack against civilians.

The video shows the drone pursuing a street vendor on a city street in the Kherson region. The man tries to move away from the drone hovering above him, cowering behind a white van as he is being pursued.

Eventually, the drone dunks on him before exploding on impact and injuring him.

Sometimes called "human safari", the deployment of remotely-operated drones against civilians has often been used by Russians to terrify residents of front line areas in Ukraine.

"The world must see this," Zelensky wrote on Telegram. "It must see every piece of evidence that Russia has gone mad, and every fact that Russian soldiers are enjoying killings and tormenting people."

The video showed a "barbaric war crime", said Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.

The safaris were a "deliberate and systemic Russian strategy," Sybiha said. "The sadist operating this drone knows full well that he is targeting a civilian."

He added the attack was part of a deliberate Russian campaign to intimidate civilians and demanded international condemnation.

The Kherson regional governor later posted a video showing the man - identified as Yuriy, a 52-year-old street vegetable vendor - speaking from a hospital bed following the drone attack.

Yuriy said he and his wife had started to lay out crates of vegetables next to his van when he heard a distinctive buzzing sound overhead.

When his wife ran away, the drone turned to him instead. He held up some heads of garlic towards the drone's camera to show the operator that he was not trying to film it.

"It could see that I had tomatoes out, some cucumbers and eggplants laid out on the floor," Yuriy said. "It even ducked under the umbrella when I was running away round the other side."

Yet the drone dove in on him and blew up. Yuriy escaped with concussion, trauma, and multiple shrapnel, his doctor said. His van was destroyed.

BBC Verify geolocated the video to a market space beside a roundabout in the Tavriiskyi district in northern Kherson. It is not clear who filmed the attack, or how - but the earliest public copy BBC Verify found was shared by a pro-Ukrainian Instagram account on Tuesday morning.

"Safari" attacks have long been carried out by Russian troops in Kherson, which sits only a few miles from the front line.

A 2025 UN report said it had found Russian armed forces "recurrently killed and injured civilians" in the area by using drones to target them.

The videos filmed by the drones before they explode on to their targets are often posted online, allowing thousands to witness the last moments of the terrified victims.

"Posting videos of civilians being killed and injured amounts to the war crime of outrages upon personal dignity," the UN said.

Additional reporting by Richard Irvine-Brown, BBC Verify

News.title: Afghan boxer arrested in Greece over discovery of Scottish woman's body in suitcase
News.content:
The man suspected of killing Scottish aid worker Elisabeth Jane Ross in Greece is 26-year-old Sharif Ahmadzai, the BBC understands.

He was arrested after the body of the 38-year-old was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, several days after she was reported missing.

Ahmadzai, who was born in Afghanistan and is a champion boxer, settled in Greece after travelling there as a teenage refugee.

He is expected to appear in court in Athens on Wednesday.

The BBC understands Ahmadzai, who left Afghanistan after being orphaned aged 15, lives in Greece with his American wife and child.

His father, a commander in the Afghan army, was shot dead and his mother and siblings were killed by a suicide bomber in Kabul.

News.title: Top Fifa official Wenger says scrapping World Cup plan 'absolutely necessary'
News.content:
Fifa's chief of global football development Arsene Wenger says scrapping the plan to have private investment in Fifa competitions was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Fifa president Gianni Infantino planned to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, with external investors able to buy stakes.

Infantino had offered Fifa's 211 member associations $40m (Â£30m) each if they backed the proposal.

But after days of criticism - including Uefa's 55 nations threatening to boycott all Fifa tournaments - Infantino was forced to withdraw the plan.

Wenger has been in a role which encompasses data analysis of the game, Fifa's online training and youth competitions since 2019.

The former Arsenal boss previously supported Infantino's proposal to play the men's World Cup every two years.

A week after Infantino's investment plan was first released, the Frenchman issued a statement through Fifa in which he demanded "transparency and integrity" from world football's governing body.

"The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side," Wenger's statement read.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger is one of 18 Fifa officials named in a document preservation letter Uefa sent to Fifa threatening legal action.

Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - is the only Fifa official to resign over the scandal, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

News.title: Bono, Eddie Vedder and Hozier among mourners at Glen Hansard's funeral
News.content:
Stars from the world of music including U2's Bono, Pearl Jam's lead singer Eddie Vedder, and Hozier, attended the funeral of Glen Hansard on Tuesday.

The 56-year-old Oscar-winning Irish singer and songwriter died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin last week.

Hansard, who shot to prominence in 1991 musical comedy film The Commitments, was long-time frontman of acclaimed rock band The Frames.

News of his sudden death shocked the music world and fans alike, with tributes being paid from the likes of Ed Sheeran and Bruce Springsteen, who said he was "heartbroken".

News.title: Justice secretary apologises to families affected by early release scheme
News.content:
Justice Secretary Alex Norris has apologised to families affected by the early release scheme, saying they were "carrying the can from previous failures".

Families, including a man whose pregnant partner died after being hit by a speeding driver, criticised the prisoner early release scheme, saying it comes "at the expense of victims".

Andy Burnham announced that prisoners convicted of rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the scheme in England and Wales. The prime minister said he wanted to exclude more, but prison overcrowding prevented this.

Calvin Buckley said he was "shocked and disappointed" the killer of his partner and unborn child could be released early.

The mother of PC Andrew Harper also said she was "devastated" to learn two men jailed after her son was killed will still be eligible.

The prime minister said making more prisoners exempt was not possible without the prison system collapsing and putting the public "at much greater risk".

Justice Secretary Alex Norris also warned a prison capacity crisis would be likely if fewer prisoners were allowed early release.

Norris later said he spoke to the families as "it is really important to express that this shouldn't be where it is".

He also said he was confident the prisons would have adequate room now that about 1,000 extra prisoners will not be released early.

"We have modelled it very carefully," he said.

PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

His family previously said they had received a letter from the Ministry of Justice confirming that two of the offenders could be included in the early release scheme.

While the driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and would not be eligible, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter could apply for early release after serving half of their sentences.

The Sentencing Act was amended in January, with the eligibility for early release based on the length of fixed sentence, rather than the type of offence.

The act already excluded some of the most serious and dangerous offenders, such as murderers serving life sentences or those on extended sentences.

But last month the prime minister promised to "review the policy" and paused the scheme after a backlash from survivors.

Announcing the changes on Monday, he said: "I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that's been caused. I've heard that loud and clear."

But PC Harper's mother Debbie Adlam, told BBC Newsnight: "It feels like we're letting Andrew down again" to hear his killers might still be eligible for release.

"We've been through the justice system, we thought we'd done as best as we could.

"Now we're standing up to fight again... so I just feel really let down, for Andrew's sake as well as ours."

She added that Norris had called her to explain the situation and apologise.

Later, on BBC Breakfast, Adlam called for more support from the probation service, stressing: "I need to know at the very, very least if they are going to be released that we're kept in mind of what's happening and we are informed".

Other families have also criticised the early release scheme.

Calvin Buckley's partner Frankie Jules-Hough and unborn child died in May 2023.

"Our justice is being taken away, I understand there's a crisis, I agree that it needs to be addressed, but not at the expense of victims," he told BBC Breakfast.

News.title: Scottish exam pass rates rise as students find out results
News.content:
Pass rates for Scottish exams have increased as students across the country received their results.

More than 148,000 learners have been finding out the results of their Nationals, Highers, Advanced Highers and Skills for Work Awards.

Qualifications Scotland - which replaced the Scottish Qualifications Authority last year after a number of controversies - said a record number of vocational and technical qualifications were awarded.

Figures show that the poverty-related attainment gap has narrowed compared with last year.

Admissions service Ucas said a record number of Scottish students aged 18 and under had been accepted into university or college. In total, 32,370 Scottish students of all ages secured places, up from 31,850 in 2025.

News.title: Surgeon struck off after wrongly connecting organs
News.content:
A doctor who botched an operation so badly it was described as "not compatible with life" has been struck off the medical register.

Dr Yasser Adly Abdel Rahman, an NHS locum surgeon from Egypt, carried out the flawed emergency bowel procedure on a young man.

It meant the contents of the patient's bowel, leaving his stomach, were re-deposited back into his stomach through a circular "closed loop", the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS) heard.

The patient was left in "uncontrollable pain" and could have died but for another surgeon correcting the error in a second operation, the misconduct hearing, sitting in Manchester, was told.

Rahman at no time considered that something may have gone wrong surgically, the tribunal heard, despite the patient's parents and other medics expressing concerns.

News.title: Fan adds 'just joking' to England World Cup win tattoo
News.content:
A man who spent Â£550 on a huge tattoo declaring England as World Cup 2026 winners has returned to the parlour to add the phrase "just joking!".

Sean Carrington, from Wigan in Greater Manchester, was so sure the Three Lions would win the World Cup that he requested a foot-long trophy homage captioned "England World Cup Winner 2026" after the nation's round of 32 victory over DR Congo.

However, the roofer has returned to the chair almost a month after England were knocked out at the semi-final stage by Argentina.

"I'm more bothered that England hasn't won the World Cup than I am to have a tattoo on my leg," the 36-year-old said, adding: "It's not bothering me. It's just a tattoo."

News.title: Fires started 'deliberately' on mountain as crews tackle blaze
News.content:
She said the fire was particularly bad on Monday night when "the smoke was so thick I couldn't breathe" and added that the firefighters had been "amazing".

Ian Putland said even with the windows closed he could smell the fire.

"I heard about it a couple of days ago, and didn't think it would affect me... but then I came out yesterday and saw ash on the car and it indicated how close the fire was," he said.

"I was then alarmed with all the fire people about."

He added that he was "frustrated that the fires had been started deliberately".

"There's the wildlife killed, people are being put in danger and it takes emergency services away. It is a real waste of resources."

Christian Hadfield, area manager at SWFRS, said crews had been at the incident since Saturday but declared it a major incident on Monday in order to protect homes in the area.

"We are putting fire breaks in and monitoring the area," he said.

He added there were reports of "pockets of deliberate fire setting" which put the crews "under really critical conditions and stretches the service".

The fire was "unpredictable and complex work", he said, and firefighters could be there "for many days to come".

News.title: Breast cancer checks missing most women under 50 who are at risk, says study
News.content:
Breast cancer is a leading cause of death in women under 50 in the UK.

Most cases - 96% - are in women over 40, while 25% are in women over 75.

Men can get breast cancer too, with about 420 new cases every year in the UK.

Natasha Finch was diagnosed with an aggressive breast cancer at just 23 despite having no known risk factors.

She has since become an advocate for breast cancer awareness and wants young women to take symptoms seriously.

"I'm six years on and still here, still winning. Going to the GP was scary, but I'm so glad I went when I did â because if I hadn't, who knows?"

"I just want to advocate for girls."

This study, by a team from Cambridge University and the Institute of Cancer Research, looks at how to predict breast cancer risk in younger women.

They used a risk calculator called Boadicea that combines factors such as family history, lifestyle, reproductive history and genetic information to give a risk score.

If all women under 50 were to have this done, they estimate about a quarter (26.5%) would be categorised as at above-average risk and referred for further assessment.

This would include a third of women under 50 (34.8%) who develop breast cancer within 10 years.

By comparison, the current Nice criteria would result in 1.4% of women under 50 being referred for further assessment, which would include just 4.4% of those women who develop breast cancer.

A main reason for the disparity, the researchers say, is because three-quarters of women (73%) under 50 who develop breast cancer within a decade have no family history of breast cancer - the key criterion in the Nice guidelines.
