News.title: Half-price rail travel extended to 18-year-olds
News.content:
Eighteen-year-olds will be able to buy half-price train tickets for most services when railcard rules are changed later this month, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.

It's an extension of the 16-17 Saver railcard which currently expires when the holder turns 18. From 17 August, they will be valid for a full year from the date of purchase.

It means 17-year-olds will be able to buy the railcard up until the day before they turn 18, making it valid until the day before they turn 19.

Seventeen-year old Lily-Mae from Blackpool told the BBC the move would save her "a few hundred [pounds] a year".

She uses the train to travel regularly from Blackpool North to Preston and Manchester.

"I have been planning to see my boyfriend and my friends, and it's just not really happened because of the price of the trains," she said.

"Also getting to college for me is hard as I go to a college in Preston, but I live in a different town, so now I won't have to save as much money to get there."

The existing rule meant more than 70,000 students each year were an average of Â£175 worse off than those in the same academic year who hadn't yet had their 18th birthday, the DfT said.

The 16-17 Saver Railcard costs Â£35 per year and entitles the holder to 50% off most train fares.

Rail minister Lord Hendy claimed this "common sense change" is "exactly what passengers should expect from the railway".

He said the change would "lower the cost of travel at a critical time for teenagers, whether they're pursuing further education, vocational pathways or getting their footing in the jobs market".

Jacqueline Starr, chief executive of industry body the Rail Delivery Group, said the change demonstrates the sector's commitment to "offering better value fares and delivering a more joined-up railway".

Kaynat Ahmad, vice president for further education at the National Union of Students, described the railcard as "essential for young people reliant on trains to get to college, work or training".

Eighteen-year-olds were already entitled to a 16-25 Railcard, but that only entitles them to a third off the cost of travel.

The government said the measure would be paid for through increased train ridership, with more passengers as a result of more people being able to access the discounted fares.

The announcement comes after the government said the cap on most single bus fares in England will be cut from Â£3 to Â£2 next year.

News.title: 'Rape list' part of misogyny girls face at school
News.content:
A group of teenage girls have said they feel "worthless" and "frightened" as a result of the extreme misogyny they regularly experience.

The students, from Tyneside, have spoken out after making a film about the language they endure at school and online.

Many comments are too explicit to share, but they include threats of violence and rape often masked as "banter". One girl described how disturbed she had been after a "rape list" was made by boys in her school.

The government said it was "taking bold and decisive action to halve violence against women and girls", with changes being introduced from September to help teachers challenge misogyny.

The North East has the highest rate of violence against women and girls in England and charities warned unchallenged attitudes could lead to abuse in early relationships.

Misogyny is defined as a contempt for, hatred of or prejudice against women.

One girl told the BBC she felt "worthless" after learning of the "rape list" made by boys in her school.

"Boys ordering girls, who they want to rape the most and then the least," she explained.

"It is frightening because you don't know people's real intentions."

News.title: Boy, 14, dies after going into water at dock
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy has drowned after going into the water at a dock in east London.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) and the Metropolitan Police searched the Millwall Outer Dock near East Ferry Road after being alerted at about 18:50 BST on Monday.

His body was recovered at about 22:30 and he was pronounced dead at the scene. His family have been informed, police said.

The Met's Det Supt Oliver Richter said: "Our thoughts remain with the family and loved ones of this young boy at this incredibly difficult time. As the warm weather continues, I would urge everyone to remember that open water can present serious dangers."

In July, the LFB urged Londoners to take extra care in the capital's waterways, in particular children, amid the continuing hot weather.

Since 2020 there have been more than 100 accidental drownings across the capital.

LFB assistant commissioner Patrick Goulbourne said: "Sadly, a teenager has drowned following an incident in Blackwall.

"Firefighters responded to reports of a teenager in the harbour and carried out a full search of the area.

"Sadly, despite the best efforts of emergency responders, the teenager was later found dead."

London Ambulance Service confirmed it had been called at 18:53 to reports of a person in the water by East Ferry Road and its crews "assisted our emergency services partners at the scene but were later stood down".

News.title: Campaigners denied appeal over Gatwick expansion
News.content:
In a 29-page ruling, they said: "We conclude that each of the grounds of appeal raised by each appellant is unarguable.

"Neither appeal has a real prospect of success. We also consider that there are no other compelling reasons for either appeal to be heard."

The two senior judges also said that the previous ruling was "detailed and thorough".

Gatwick is the UK's second busiest airport and one of the busiest single-runway airports in the world.

The expansion will allow the site to be used for the departures of narrow-bodied planes such as Airbus A320s and Boeing 737s.

Following the decision, Barclay said: "We are very disappointed with the Court's decision. We took this challenge as far as we could because we believed that the decision to allow Gatwick to expand was fundamentally flawed.

"It was not supported by government policy, would only serve to line the pockets of the airport and airlines, and would do so at the expense of local residents and the climate."

Cagne said: "Residents should be immensely proud of what they have achieved in holding Gatwick Airport's shareholders to account.

"This proposed new runway will come at a significant cost to both the taxpayer and the planet."

News.title: Star Wars dubbed in Welsh for the first time to celebrate landmark anniversary
News.content:
Star Wars is to be dubbed into Welsh for the first time as the classic film prepares to celebrate its 50th anniversary next year.

Welsh language broadcaster S4C and Creative Wales announced the project, in partnership with Lucasfilm and Disney, at the National Eisteddfod on Tuesday.

The Welsh language version of Episode IV - A New Hope will broadcast on S4C and its platforms from Christmas Day.

Actor Matthew Rhys will voice Han Solo, with Rhys Ifans as Obi-Wan Kenobi, and Aimee-Ffion Edwards as Princess Leia.

Star Wars veteran Mark Lewis Jones, who portrayed Captain Moden Canady in Episode VIII - The Last Jedi, will take on the role of Darth Vader and Osian Morgan will voice Luke Skywalker.

Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd is directed by Ellyn Stern and produced by Michael Kohn, director of distribution operations at Lucasfilm.

"We're really excited about this project for many reasons," Kohn said.

"I've been involved in a few indigenous dubs of Star Wars over the years that aim to preserve and revitalise interest in learning the language.

"The chance to celebrate the Welsh language through Star Wars is one we couldn't pass up."

News.title: Ex neo-Nazi activist selected as Tory candidate
News.content:
A man who was jailed over his neo-Nazi activism will stand as a Tory candidate in council elections after being offered a "second chance" by the party.

Joshua Bonehill-Paine spent three years in prison for posting antisemitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally and a year later he was also convicted of racially harassing then-Labour MP Luciana Berger.

Bonehill-Payne has been selected to stand in the new Somerset Council seat of Crewkerne South in 2027. He said he wanted to "give back" to a community which had supported him.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said he had "shown contrition for his crimes" but the Board of Deputies of British Jews said the move "beggars belief".

Reform UK has regained its lead over Labour in a fresh poll that raises questions over the longevity of the so-called ‘Burnham bounce’.

The new prime minister has been credited with ending the run that saw Nigel Farage boast his party had led in the polls for more than a year after two surveys put Labour on top while three had the party tied with Reform, days after Andy Burnham entered Downing Street.

But a new YouGov poll puts Reform in front again, with 23 per cent vote share to Labour’s 22 per cent.

Reform has overtaken Labour in a new poll ( AFP/Getty )

In a similar YouGov survey last week, Labour and Reform were both tied at 22 per cent.

The result comes after a difficult few weeks for Mr Farage, who has struggled to explain a £5m gift from crypto-billionaire Christopher Harborne, which prompted a parliamentary sleaze probe. At the same time Labour’s Bev Craig won the Greater Manchester mayoralty election, trouncing Reform.

But Dr Patrick English, YouGov’s head of elections and political data, suggested voters had yet to be won over by the new Labour government.

He told The Telegraph there had certainly been a “positive response from the British public to Labour’s removal of Keir Starmer and replacement with Andy Burnham, who is currently the most positively rated party leader that we are measuring”.

But he warned that even though Burnham leads the pollster’s favourability ratings “he is not hugely popular”, adding: “So I don’t think we should expect a massive surge in Labour support, and I would caution expectations in that regard because the British public still don’t think that the government is doing a brilliant job.”

“They still don’t think they’re addressing their concerns around the cost of living and around immigration, and they’re going to want to see actual improvement and actual changes in their day-to-day lives before they start giving Labour more reward in the polls and more reward at the ballot box.”

Before Mr Burnham became prime minister, Reform had led in more than 300 consecutive surveys since April 2025.

But a Survation poll last Tuesday put Labour on top with 26 per cent, up one point, with Farage’s party on 24 per cent, down two points.

That result followed a More in Common poll released on Monday which put Labour ahead with 28 per cent compared to Reform’s 24 per cent.

Mr Farage is currently campaigning to win back his parliamentary seat in the Clacton by-election, after he dramatically resigned to trigger a vote.

The move was in protest at what he claimed was his treatment over the investigation into a £5m donation from Mr Harborne. He is also facing questions over gifts and support he received from convicted money launderer George Cottrell.

News.title: 13 best clothes steamers for quickly removing creases
News.content:
Your questions about the best clothes steamers answered

What is the best clothes steamer?

If you want one steamer that performs well across a full wardrobe, the Russell Hobbs steam genie vacusteam is the best all-rounder. It heats up quickly and is powerful to use so you can get each garment done with fewer strokes. For travel, I’d recommend the Lakeland foldable clothes steamer, which is surprisingly powerful for its size. For home use or larger loads, the Fridja F10 was impressive, with different settings to quickly steam a variety of fabrics.

How I tested clothes steamers

Having crease-free clothing is paramount to me, so I took great pride in testing a broad range of different steamers to find the best options. When testing, I considered the following:

Effectiveness: To gauge effectiveness, I put each steamer to the test against a range of common fabrics, from cotton shirts to linen trousers and delicate silks. I paid close attention to how well they tackled both deep-set, laundry-basket wrinkles and lighter, everyday creases.

To gauge effectiveness, I put each steamer to the test against a range of common fabrics, from cotton shirts to linen trousers and delicate silks. I paid close attention to how well they tackled both deep-set, laundry-basket wrinkles and lighter, everyday creases. Efficiency: I timed everything from initial heat-up speed to how long a full water tank lasted during continuous use. I also considered the ergonomics of each model – how comfortable it felt to hold and manoeuvre over garments for extended periods.

I timed everything from initial heat-up speed to how long a full water tank lasted during continuous use. I also considered the ergonomics of each model – how comfortable it felt to hold and manoeuvre over garments for extended periods. Results: Beyond simply banishing wrinkles, I paid close attention to the final finish. Did clothes look crisp and box-fresh, or were they left feeling slightly damp? I also checked for any spitting or water marks on the fabric, and how well the steam worked to refresh items and remove any lingering odours from wear.

Iron vs clothes steamer: which is better?

Having tested both irons and clothes steamers extensively, I’d say your best tool for removing creases depends on what you actually need day to day.

Steam irons are more powerful, especially steam generator models. When I was tackling big loads like school uniforms or bedding, an iron was far more effective. It presses fabric flat, gives a crisp finish and deals with deep creases much faster. You also can’t use a clothes steamer on bedsheets or large items in the same way.

Clothes steamers, on the other hand, are much more convenient. I found them quicker for everyday use. You can leave clothes on a hanger and smooth out creases in minutes, without setting up an ironing board. They’re also gentler on delicate fabrics and great for freshening up clothes between washes.

In short: if you want precision and power, go for an iron. If you want speed and convenience, a steamer is the better choice.

How to use a clothes steamer?

According to the experts, it all starts with what you put into tank. Stylist Lauren Paxton explains: “I love M&S ironing mists and waters, which help reduce creases. But it’s very important to empty the tank after each clean, so there’s no stagnant water damaging your clothes.”

Celebrity stylist Rebecca Kahane agrees and says: “For the best results, use distilled water. It helps prolong the life of the steamer and ensures a cleaner, more consistent steam. I don’t always have it on hand, but I try to avoid tap water when possible.”

The pros also suggest different steaming techniques to simply hanging up the garment and working vertically. Kahane adds: “For stubborn wrinkles, I start by steaming the inside of the garment first, then move to the outside. If the fabric becomes too damp, I let it dry slightly before going back in to finish. A stylist trick I love is placing a thin sock over the steamer head to prevent water spots, especially while it’s heating up and may spit a bit.”

What type of clothes steamer should I go for?

Typically, garment steamers come in two types: upright and handheld. While both designs are able to tackle creases effectively, there are a few key differences between them:

Upright steamers – These models are generally far more powerful than handheld steamers and, as such, are better suited to larger or heavy-duty jobs. They also have sizeable water tanks, so you can steam for longer without refilling, and often feature built-in hangers, too. However, it’s worth considering that upright steamers tend to be more expensive and bigger in size, which makes them less portable.

What fabrics should not be steamed?

While some steamers are suitable for use on all fabrics, others shouldn’t be used on extremely delicate materials, so it’s always best to check with the manufacturer before you get started. According to clothes steamer brand Fridja, these gadgets are typically very versatile and capable of removing creases on a wide range of fabrics, including natural fibres such as linen, silk, cotton and even wool.

If you’re still unsure, the brand recommends using a delicate fabric guard to help prevent damage. Meanwhile, synthetic materials such as polyester, nylon and acrylic are typically very easy to steam using all clothes steamers.

News.title: The economy is on Trump’s agenda as he visits Newsom’s turf in California
News.content:
President Donald Trump is making a rare visit to California and Nevada this week to contrast his policies with Democrats on the economy, border security, and crime, aiming to strengthen Republican support for the upcoming November elections.

Trump is struggling with voter confidence on the economy, as an AP-NORC poll shows only 32% approval for his economic handling, with 69% of Americans describing the economy as 'poor' and citing high stress from the cost of essentials.

In California, Trump will attend a Republican National Committee fundraising dinner and is anticipated to criticize Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom, a prominent political rival and potential 2028 presidential candidate, continuing their history of public disagreements.

During his Nevada stop, Trump will discuss the economy, while state Democrats are actively campaigning to associate him with Governor Joe Lombardo and rising costs, highlighting local issues such as housing shortages and increasing energy demands.

Trump's efforts to promote his income tax cuts and a manufacturing renaissance are challenged by high interest rates, elevated gasoline prices, ongoing tariffs, and a national housing shortage, often causing his economic speeches to shift focus to political adversaries.

News.title: Joanna Page calls husband ‘fifth child’ in clash over family holiday
News.content:
Joanna Page criticised her husband James Thornton for being her “fifth child” as the couple clashed over a family holiday.

The Gavin and Stacey star discussed a recent trip away on her podcast Lush!, where she chastised Thornton, whom she has been married to for 23 years, for his “lack of help”.

“Have I got to do everything?”, she asked her husband, who she claimed was doing nothing whilst she was helping the kids pack their beach bags for a pool day.

After Thornton stated that it was Page’s job to “do the bags”, she fired back: “Why can’t you? Is there something wrong with you?”

News.content:

Big oil companies continue to book massive profits as fighting in Iran disrupts energy markets and sends oil and gasoline prices sharply higher.

Six of Europe’s largest oil companies posted combined first-quarter profits of $22 billion, more than 40% higher than last year. Profits at BP, based in London, more than doubled to $3.9 billion in the second quarter, the company said Tuesday.

And Saudi Aramco reported a 44% year-on-year increase in second-quarter net profit that reached $32.69 billion, driven by higher crude oil, refined products and chemicals prices.

The supercharged performances from big oil in Europe and the Middle East follow reports of enormous profits from the largest U.S. oil drillers last week.

As the conflict has dragged on, high oil prices have driven up the cost of gasoline, jet fuel and diesel, which has led to higher shipping costs. In the West, filling up the car or buying a plane ticket is costing consumers more. But the situation in parts of Asia are more dire because the region depends more heavily on fuel exported through the Strait of Hormuz. Fuel supplies have run low in some countries, leading to rationing and sporadic closures of schools and government offices.

Despite oil prices falling to their lowest level in three weeks Tuesday, big U.S. energy companies drew the ire of President Donald Trump, who criticized them this week for their outsized profits.

Trump said he’s not happy with Chevron and Exxon Mobil, though energy prices skyrocketed only after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in late February, and the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed off to tanker traffic.

About 20% of the world’s oil typically flows through the strait.

“They made too much money, too much money,” Trump said Monday. “They ought to give some of that back to the public, and they better cut the retail price.”

Exxon Mobil on Friday reported that its second quarter profits doubled to $14.5 billion, boosted by record diesel production. The oil giant, based in Spring, Texas, brought in $116 billion in revenue, up 42%.

Chevron, based in Houston, nearly quadrupled its profits to $12 billion and revenue jumped 56% to more than $70 billion.

On Tuesday, the price of U.S. crude oil fell 5.4%, or $4.36, to $75.98 per barrel. The sharp decline followed comments by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who told CNBC that the U.S. and Iran “may have a deal today or tomorrow to open the Strait.”

Oil prices for U.S. crude are down from around $92 a barrel in late July, but still more than 13% higher than when the conflict with Iran started.

Brent crude, the international standard, fell 4.9% to $83.87 per barrel.

A resolution to the Iran conflict, which has lasted more than five months, could give oil shippers the ability to send vessels out of the Persian Gulf, where tankers of oil and other products have been trapped during the fighting.

An England fan who prematurely crowned England as World Cup winners in a tattoo has had his new artwork amended.

Sean Carrington spent £550 on a leg tattoo of the World Cup trophy above the words "England World Cup Winner 2026" after The Three Lions’ 2-1 win over DR Congo in the round of 32.

The 36-year-old was so convinced Thomas Tuchel's side would go all the way before Argentina prematurely ended England’s chances of World Cup glory in a 2-1 defeat.

Now the roofer has returned to Holy Trinity Tattoo Studio in Standish to add “Just joking” underneath.

Following his second trip to the tattoo parlour, he told the BBC: "I'm more bothered that England hasn't won the World Cup than I am to have a tattoo on my leg”.

He added: "It's not bothering me. It's just a tattoo."

Sean Carrington does not regret his tattoo of the World Cup trophy above the words ‘England World Cup Winner 2026’ ( Social media )

Carrington said he did not regret getting the original tattoo and he "wouldn't have done anything differently".

He said he was happy with the result of the extra line added to his tattoo and remarked how it was "sound", adding: "I didn't really feel it."

Jamie Taylor, the parlour's manager, said the tattoo would normally have cost about £100, but they had decided to do the correction for free.

When asked whether he has plans for any more tattoos, Carrington did not rule out the possibility of getting another football-related tribute in the future.

"I don't plan any tattoo, it's just if it pops in my head," he said.

Holy Trinity Tattoo’s Facebook page shared a video of the new amendment which said: “This is exactly why tattoo artists tell you to wait.”

The venue added: “Well… this aged well.

“Last month our customer was so confident he had ‘England World Cup Winners 2026’ tattooed.

“Fast forward to today… and he’s been back for a little update.

“‘Just joking.’

“At least he’s got a good sense of humour! Fair play for owning it.”

After England’s late defeat to Argentina in the semi-finals, Tuchel’s side went on to finish the tournament in third place, beating France 6-4 in the ‘Bronze Final’ in Miami.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
For many the 100m is the Blue Riband event the one everyone wants to watch and the race that steals all the headlines. For these Commonwealth Games, however, tonight’s mile race is the one that has grabbed all the attention – and it is not hard to see why.

Josh Kerr, fresh from his new world record of 3:42.66 (a time that beat a mark that had stood since 1999) takes on fellow Scot Jake Wightman and Australia’s new superstar Cameron Myers. Three great runners over a distance that evokes sepia-tinted memories of Roger Bannister and the seminal four-minute mark.

Some of you may be wondering why the mile is back at an international event. Well, Seb Coe, the president of World Athletics and someone who broke the mile record three times, says the race distance is easy to understand and resonates with fans. And, coming on the back of Kerr’s world record, who can argue with him?

This is the first time the mile has been run at the games since 1966 and the hope is that tonight’s final matches the Miracle Mile run in 1954. Earlier that year Bannister broke the four-minute barrier, only for Australia’s John Landy to go lower with a time of 3:58.0 soon after. The Games in Vancouver were the first time two sub-four minuters had gone head-to-head. And the race didn’t disappoint – Bannister beating Landy with a time of 3:58.8 minutes. The Australian also ran under four minutes, making it the first time two men had done so in the same race.

Obviously all three of the expected main protagonists will go well under four minutes, but if they can recreate the drama of the 1954 final then we’ll have a race to savour.

Stay here for all the action with the gun set to go off at 8.55.

Sports.title: Chelsea files: Blues out to exorcise infamous ghost on Sunday, shirt sponsor woes continue and Maignan transter update
Sports.content:
CHELSEA will have the chance to bury a few ghosts in Malaysia on Sunday.

Or one, at least.



Because the chief executive of local opponents Johor Darul Ta’zim is none other than former Liverpool star Luis Garcia.

The Spaniard scored what then Chelsea boss Jose Mourinho called the “ghost goal” at Anfield in May 2005 to decide a tense Champions League semi-final second leg.



In the fourth minute, Garcia jabbed the ball goalwards after Blues goalkeeper Petr Cech had brought down Milan Baros.

Although William Gallas cleared the effort, the near-side linesman ruled it had crossed the line.



Liverpool held on to secure a 1-0 aggregate win and went on to beat AC Milan in the final in Istanbul.

Garcia, now 47, spent many years as a TV pundit after hanging up his boots in 2016.

But in 2025, he agreed to take charge of Johor.

The club had been formed in 2012 in a radical revamp of football in the state of Johor, led by Crown Prince Tunku Ismail Idris, son of Malaysia’s ruling sultan.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Prince became the club’s owner in 2016.

Talks with Garcia were set up by fellow Spaniard Kiko Insa, who had become an agent after a journeyman career that ended at Johor.

Johor claimed Malaysia’s domestic Treble for the first time in Garcia’s first season in charge and have won the last 12 league titles.

But they lost in the quarter-finals of the AFC Champions League to reigning champions Al-Ahli.



And in goal for the Saudi side was Edouard Mendy, who was in Chelsea’s 2021 Champions League-winning side.

Sunday’s match at the Larkin Stadium is a chance for the Blues to gain some direct revenge over Garcia.

BLANK SLATE

IT is a year since Chelsea parted company with chief revenue officer Casper Stylsvig amid rows over the failure to secure a lucrative front-of-shirt sponsor.



But unless something happens very soon, the Blues will go into a new season for the fourth time under the current owners without a deal.

It is simply extraordinary that a big-name Premier League club, led by high-flying finance gurus, has “lost” tens of millions in revenue by not replacing previous long-term backer Three.

The mobile phone firm’s £40m-per-year contract ended at the conclusion of the 2022-23 season, the first year of the BlueCo regime.

Last season’s temporary fix was a deal with little-known AI firm IFS, which saw the company pay double-digit millions to have their name on the shirts from February until the end of the campaign.

IFS will continue as longer-term partners, but a blue-chip company willing to match the Blues’ demands remains elusive.



Chelsea are in a much weaker negotiating position than 12 months ago, when they had just won the Club World Cup and were preparing to return to the Champions League.

Even then, though, no-one was prepared to stump up the £60-65 million per year BlueCo wanted.

With no European football at all in 2026/27, the club cannot offer the same top-level visibility for a brand.

The Premier League ban on gambling firms being shirt sponsors has narrowed options for the Blues and other clubs.

Chelsea are not alone in lacking a backer barely two weeks before the new campaign begins, with Champions League participants Aston Villa among those still searching.



But fans remain frustrated the financial and commercial geniuses in charge of the club have still not secured a key source of revenue.

MIK DROP

CHELSEA have repeatedly denied any ongoing interest in AC Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan.

But if they have changed their mind again, then Saturday’s friendly in Jakarta between the two clubs would be a good chance to re-open talks.



Milan are said to be unconcerned about their captain recently deleting all mention of the club from his Instagram account, although you can never be sure of the truth in an era when social media makes kids out of grown adults.

Maignan himself is not due to be in Indonesia for the Chelsea game, as he and fellow France international Adrien Rabiot are not due to report back for pre-season until August 12, after their run to the semi-finals of the World Cup.

Mike Penders has joined up with the Blues in Hong Kong, though, after his own stint across the Atlantic.

Penders was Belgium’s No 3 ‘keeper behind former Chelsea star Thibaut Courtois and Manchester United’s Senne Lammens and remains uncapped after not playing a minute at the tournament.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Xabi Alonso will surely give Penders his club debut in one or more of the three remaining fixtures of the Asian tour.



Only then will Alonso be able to gain a better idea of whether he wants the club to go shopping for another ‘keeper or is willing to give Penders, back from loan at sister club Strasbourg, the chance to challenge Robert Sanchez.

Sports.title: Newcastle ‘make Premier League star’s brother top target to replace Bruno Guimaraes’ as Arsenal close in on transfer
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE have reportedly identified Felix Nmecha as their preferred replacement for Bruno Guimaraes.

The Magpies are set to lose their captain before the new Premier League season kicks off, with Arsenal poised to sign him.



It has been widely reported that Guimaraes will join the Gunners in a deal worth £80million.

While nothing has been officially confirmed, Newcastle are already on the hunt for his replacement.



And French outlet L’Equipe reports that Nmecha is the No1 target.

The midfielder, who appeared for Germany at the World Cup earlier this summer, is the younger brother of Leeds United forward Lukas Nmecha.

He currently plays for Borussia Dortmund, having joined from Wolfsburg three years ago.

Prior to his time in Germany, Nmecha graduated from Manchester City‘s academy and made three first team appearances.

It has not yet been disclosed how much Newcastle would have to pay to sign the 25-year-old.

However, the Magpies have allegedly been informed about Dortmund’s main demands.

Manchester United are also believed to be interested in Nmecha as they continue searching for a new midfielder.

A return to Man City has also been rumoured.

Sports.title: Arsenal on brink of total Bruno Guimaraes agreement with Newcastle with all parties wanting transfer done
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are on the brink of landing Bruno Guimaraes in a blockbuster deal.

The midfielder, 28, jetted into Spain for Newcastle’s pre-season training camp yesterday.



But Guimaraes’ heart was set on joining Arsenal ahead of showdown talks with incoming Magpies chief Matthias Jaissle.

And the Brazilian has moved to within touching distance of getting his wish.



Arsenal and Newcastle have edged towards reaching a total agreement over a transfer.

The Magpies initially insisted offers would not be entertained for their skipper as they desperately fought to keep him.



But Newcastle have been forced into a U-turn after Guimaraes, who played a key role in Brazil’s World Cup campaign before they crashed out in the last-16, made it clear that he wants to quit.

And there is now a desire among all parties to find a resolution instead of allowing the transfer saga to drag on.

Guimaraes is waiting for Newcastle to give him the green light to travel to North London for a medical before completing the mega-money switch.

The former Lyon man made 41 appearances in all competitions last season, notching nine goals and eight assists along the way.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Guimaraes wrote his name into the Newcastle history books as he wore the captain’s armband when they ended a 70-year wait for silverware by winning the Carabao Cup in March 2025.

But he is now in line to follow the likes of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali – along with boss Eddie Howe – in heading through the exit door this summer.

Arsenal bolstered their attacking options with the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis last month.

Illan Meslier has also arrived at the Emirates Stadium to provide cover for No1 David Raya.

Sports.content:
ALEJANDRO GARNACHO was forced off with a bloodied mouth just two weeks after signing for Aston Villa.

The Argentine winger, 22, completed his season-long loan switch to Villa Park from Chelsea on July 23.



He made his debut against the Indonesia All Stars and was included in the starting XI again against BG Pathum.

The former Manchester United man needed medical treatment on the field before having to make way due to the facial injury.

Villa led 2-0 at half-time thanks to goals from Emi Buendia and Victor Lindelof.

And Boubacar Kamara added a third in the second half.

There was another injury concern for the Premier League side when John McGinn landed awkwardly and appeared to jar his knee, with Unai Emery taking no risks and taking him off.

And eventually the match did start 30 minutes later than planned.

Garnacho is desperate to get his career back on track under Emery this season.

He swapped Old Trafford for Stamford Bridge last summer for £40million.

Sports.title: Mykhailo Mudryk found love and hit gym in Chelsea exile – now the real heavy lifting of reviving his career begins
Sports.content:
MYKHAILO MUDRYK has kept himself in good enough shape to bench press his girlfriend.

And the Chelsea winger has plenty more heavy lifting to do to revive his career after nearly 20 months out of the game.



Mudryk gained a new celebrity partner, influencer and actor Jordyn Jones, and, for a while at least, a new haircut, during his enforced absence.

But the Ukrainian has a massive challenge on his hands to prove wrong the critics who believed he was the Blues’ most expensive mistake even before he copped a ban for failing a drugs test in October 2024.



Perhaps if Mudryk shows the same determination he used to pursue Jones, he will be able to turn his on-field fortunes around.

She has 8.7million followers on Instagram and that is where their romance began.



Last September Mudryk commented on one of her videos, asking the online audience: “Guys, should I try?”.

Then he messaged Jones directly and said: “Let’s meet in Paris. I’ve got 2 tickets to Disneyland, don’t want to go alone.”

The 26-year-old American had to be won over, even temporarily blocking Mudryk after he bombarded her with messages.

But by March this year, after some flirty exchanges, Jones had given in to his charms.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

She posted an image of his original invitation to the theme park with a photo of herself outside the gates, tagging Mudryk and saying: “Fast forward six months. I’m glad I unblocked you.”

Jones also posted pictures of herself wearing a Chelsea scarf and shirt.

In April Mudryk, 25, proved he had not been neglecting his physical strength during his time away from the pitch.

Jones posted a video of her boyfriend lying on a weight bench and lifting her up and down.



One Chelsea fan described the feat as “iconic”.

But it is fair to say Mudryk did not live up to that description in the time between his arrival at Stamford Bridge in January 2023 and his ban.

Chelsea beat off competition from Arsenal to sign the Ukraine international for an initial £62m, rising to £88m, in their extraordinary first winter window under their big-spending new owners.

But he managed only 10 goals in 73 appearances before his career was put on hold.

Three of those strikes came in Chelsea’s Conference League campaign of 2024/25, including the second in a 2-0 win at German club Heidenheim which turned out to be Mudryk’s last appearance for the club before he was banned.



In December 2024, Mudryk confirmed he had tested positive for a banned substance in an out-of-competition test in October.

It later emerged the drug concerned was meldonium, the same heart medication which led to tennis star Maria Sharapova serving a 15-month ban.

Mudryk was provisionally suspended from December and finally charged by the Football Association in May 2025.



In that same month, Mudryk was pictured in the Polish city of Wroclaw on the eve of Chelsea’s Conference League final against Real Betis.

The terms of his suspension stopped him from training at Chelsea’s Surrey headquarters and working with any club staff.

But his presence in Wroclaw sparked speculation he would link up with his team-mates.

It did not happen, however, and Mudryk’s long, lonely wait continued. He had received the maximum four-year ban for failing the drugs test and then launched an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Apart from his romance with Jones, he kept a low profile while his legal team fought his corner.



In November 2025, a photo emerged of him with dark hair, as opposed to his trademark blond, when he met up with friends from Ukrainian football.

It is understood Mudryk worked hard behind the scenes to maintain his physical condition.

In March this year, he posted a video of him training at Uxbridge FC’s Honeycroft stadium, which he had hired out privately.



Then last month he shared footage of him belting a ball into the top corner during a session in Austria, with the caption: “Stay tuned.”

Sure enough, last week Mudryk was given permission to resume his career after reaching an agreement with the FA, CAS and the World Anti-Doping Agency. He always insisted he had never knowingly taken a banned substance.

The low concentration of meldonium detected in his original sample would no longer trigger an adverse anti-doping finding.

In a statement on Instagram, Mudryk thanked his family, friends, Chelsea and legal team for their help and support during “the most difficult period of my career”.

He immediately flew out to join the Blues on the Asian leg of their pre-season tour.



Privately, Mudryk and his team know it will take time to get up to speed with the demands of top-level training and playing after so long out of the game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Coventry, managed by Chelsea legend Frank Lampard, are among three Premier League clubs interested in giving him the chance to prove his worth.

And Jones can tell them just how committed Mudryk is when given a challenge.

Sports.title: Cape Verde manager resigns after famous World Cup campaign and instantly takes club job
Sports.content:
CAPE VERDE’s manager has resigned to take on a new club role following the World Cup.

Bubista, full name Pedro Leitão Brito, guided Cape Verde‘s incredible World Cup campaign in North America.



The minnows qualified for the tournament for the first time ever but were not given much of a prayer in terms of results.

However, they immediately stuck it to their doubters by earning a surprise draw with Spain in the first game – arguably one of the biggest upsets ever given the 65 ranking spots between them and even crazier considering Spain went on to win the tournament.



They then followed that up by drawing with Uruguay and then drawing with Saudi Arabia and qualifying for the Round of 32, where they were drawn against Argentina.

Bubista’s side performed valiantly – twice coming from behind and taking Lionel Messi and Co into extra time before they were eliminated 3-2.



But just weeks after the tournament, Bubista has become the head club of Moroccan football club RS Berkane.

A club statement announced he had signed a two-year contract.

It added: “This signing comes as part of the club’s ongoing sporting project and its commitment to bolstering its competitive ambitions both domestically and continentally.

“It relies on high technical expertise and distinguished experience in global— and particularly African — football, while providing opportunities to nurture and elevate our brilliant young talents.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“RS Berkane wishes the new manager every success in leading the team, achieving our shared goals, and bringing joy to the Orange fans in the coming period.”

Bubista won Africa’s coach of the year award for his efforts in getting Cape Verde to the World Cup for the first time in 2025.

He had managed a quartet of Cape Verdean clubs in Mindelense, Académica do Mindelo, Sporting Praia and Batuque before taking the national team role in 2020.

Berkane won the Moroccan league in 2025 and finished runners up in the league this year, while they also reached the CAF Champions League semi-finals last season.

REAL MADRID winger Vinicius Jr has publicly spoken out for the first time since being linked with a move to Arsenal.

“That’s pre-season for you – we’ve got to be ready.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part
Sports.content:
Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part

The England captain will head back to his club in the next few days and Bayern will immediately resume talks over a new contract that will keep the striker in the Bundesliga beyond 2027

View 3 Images Harry Kane has had three very productive seasons with Bayern Munich (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Just over nine years ago, Harry Kane mildly surprised a small gathering of reporters when he declared winning the Ballon d’Or to be one of his prime ambitions. Nothing wrong with aiming high, of course. But, at the time, Kane was a 23-year-old striker who had made 17 appearances for his country and had scored five goals.

‌



His numbers with Spurs were very good - 78 goals in 113 Premier League appearances - but he had only been an established top-flight player for three seasons. But Kane believed in himself and lifting that Ballon d’Or is a realistic prospect when the awards ceremony, for the first time in its history, comes to London in October.

‌



Carabao Cup draw confirmed as final fixtures announced for round one READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Bookmakers do not normally get these sorts of things wrong and every odds-maker has Kane as the favourite to become the seventh British player to receive the accolade. The influence of the World Cup, though, should not be under-estimated.

‌



Some of the 100 journalists who make the choice could well forgive Rodri an injury-interrupted and otherwise mediocre season with his club for his imperious role in Spain’s summer triumph. Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe would appear to be the only other realistic contenders.

And they are worthy contenders. If Kane does not win the 2026 edition, he will have the award in his sights for next year - a year with no major international tournaments.

And if he stays at Bayern Munich, goals are a guarantee. In three seasons in Germany, he has 146 in 147 appearances. If he moved to Barcelona - a switch that seems slightly fanciful but has been mooted reasonably strongly - goals would be a guarantee.

‌



View 3 Images Rodri won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and is a strong contender for this year's award (Image: Getty Images)

Kane is not coming back to the Premier League any time soon, we can be fairly certain of that. He will report back for training with Bayern after the Bundesliga champions have returned from a pre-season trip to Korea and Hong Kong on Saturday.

Contract talks will immediately resume, as his current deal expires in the summer of 2027. And quite frankly, it is hard to see why Kane would not want to extend his agreement.

‌



He could ask for a release clause at the end of next season if he feels he might have the urge to come back and break the Premier League goalscoring record - he is currently 47 short of Alan Shearer’s total of 260 - but he seems extremely content in Bavaria. Plus, the style of play, the quality of play, the guarantee of competing for honours on all fronts, are all factors that will help him stay in top shape for the international challenges that still lie ahead, most notably leading England into Euro 2028.

He turned 33 a week ago but Kane has looked a better, all-round player for his time in Munich. He was certainly more impressive for England at World Cup 2026 than he was at either Euro 2024 or World Cup 2022. He is not unusual but playing in a dominant team suits him.

View 3 Images Harry Kane has plenty of international challenges left despite his World Cup disappointment (Image: Getty Images)

‌



When he sits down with his advisers and the Bayern hierarchy in the next week, there will, of course, be no escaping the relevance of his age. But over the past few years, the longevity of marquee players - and of strikers, in particular - will have probably had a bearing on his plans.

Since his 34th birthday, Kane’s predecessor at Bayern, Robert Lewandowski, has scored 125 club goals. Kane could return to the Premier League as a 35-year-old - in two seasons’ time - and still fancy his chances of beating Shearer’s number.

But before then, he will have his eyes on another individual accolade. And if the Ballon d’Or does not come his way on the 70th anniversary of the award (the first one, in 1956, was won by Stanley Matthews, hence why the ceremony is in London), you can guarantee he will be a contender again if he stays at Bayern Munich. The Premier League and Shearer’s record are going to have to wait.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands new job in football following retirement
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands new job in football following retirement

Anthony Taylor called time on his refereeing career last month, but he's already found a new position that will see him take his wealth of experience as a match official abroad

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor retired after 20-year refereeing career (Image: Ayman Aref/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Anthony Taylor has landed a new job in football just weeks after announcing his retirement from professional refereeing. The former Premier League match official has been appointed the director of elite refereeing for the Turkish Football Federation (TFF).

‌



Taylor, 47, hung up his whistle after his last match at this summer's World Cup, taking charge of Spain's 1-0 win against Portugal in the round of 16. But now he's back in football with the TFF.

‌



"I am delighted to be joining the Turkish Football Federation and very much looking forward to beginning this new role," Taylor said. "Elite refereeing has been at the centre of my professional life for many years, and this appointment gives me the opportunity to use that experience in a different way."

‌



His appointment comes 10 months after the conclusion of a five-year investigation which found that 371 of 571 match officials in Turkey had betting accounts. TFF president Ibrahim Haciosmanoglu stated at the time: "If we want to bring Turkish football to the place it deserves, we have to clean up whatever dirt there is."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Some of the clean-up job will be given to Taylor, who refereed 831 matches over a 20-year career. "I am excited by the Federation's ambitions for its match officials and by the opportunity to help shape the strategic and technical development of its refereeing programme," Taylor added.

‌



"There is already a great deal of talent and commitment within Turkey, and I look forward to working with colleagues across the Federation to build on those foundations and support the continued development of referees at every stage of the elite pathway.

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor will bring his expertise to Turkey (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

"Retiring from elite refereeing was a significant decision, but I was always clear that I wanted to remain closely involved in the game and contribute to the future of officiating. This is an exciting opportunity to begin that next chapter, and I look forward to getting started."

‌



Taylor, from Altrincham, worked as a prison guard before becoming a professional referee. The 47-year-old suggested when announcing his retirement that the 'intense' pressure and 'constant' scrutiny had played a role in his decision.

In May 2023, Taylor and his family were harassed by Roma supporters at Budapest Airport following their Europa League final defeat to Sevilla and criticism from then-Roma manager Jose Mourinho. Taylor revealed last year that his family no longer came to watch matches that he refereed.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso's task at Chelsea: 46-player squad, baffling transfers and confusing hierarchy
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso knew perfectly well what he was signing himself up for when he agreed to become the next Chelsea manager.

"I had a view of Chelsea from the outside," Alonso told reporters while on Chelsea's pre-season tour of Australia. "I could see the positives and my concerns so I addressed them.

"We had the same ideas, the same analysis, to start building momentum together. That is why we are taking these steps together and making decisions to build a good team."

We don't need to ask Alonso what view he had of Chelsea before he arrived, because the picture has been painted very clearly over the past few years. It is one defined by muddied thinking and a chaotic approach, which comes together to create the biggest circus in the Premier League.

‌



Alonso is only in the early stages of his Chelsea career and will obviously need time to stamp his authority on things and turn around a side which finished a lowly 10th in the Premier League last season. Yet, despite having the title of manager, rather than head coach, he will have to do so within the same parameters of his predecessors Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea sanctions reveal same punishment for sexual misconduct and ticket transferring READ MORE :

In the post-Roman Abramovich era, of which Todd Boehly has become the gormless face, Chelsea have become the most puzzling of entities where more confusion and baffling mismanagement is only around the corner. After all, this is a club that, defying convention, have five sporting directors.

It is a club, that at the time of writing, have 46 first-team players listed on their website. A club who have, despite their vast swathes of players, spent approximately £336million in the summer transfer window so far, with more no doubt to come.

‌



And a club which has, partly on Alonso's say-so, changed their youth-first transfer approach to sign 35-year-old Danny Welbeck and 36-year-old Jordan Henderson.

View 4 Images Jordan Henderson has joined Chelsea (Image: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC)

Welbeck's arrival means Chelsea currently have six senior strikers. Of them only Joao Pedro is assured of his position. Liam Delap, a £30m signing last summer, could be shipped out, Nicolas Jackson is looking for a new team after spending last season on loan at Bayern Munich and Marc Guiu is on the transfer list having been recalled from Sunderland last season due to injuries.

It is a muddled picture entirely in-keeping with Chelsea's modus operandi. Last summer, Maresca felt he had no other choice than to create a 'bomb squad', featuring the highly-paid group of Raheem Sterling, Axel Disasi, Joao Felix and Ben Chilwell.

‌



This summer it is Alonso who has the unenviable task of trying to work out which players he wants, which ones he doesn't and how to create some kind of squad unity amidst it all. Marc Cucurella may be gone after his frank criticism of the hierarchy, but senior players Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo - who both publicly flirted with rival clubs during the slide under Rosenior - remain.

View 4 Images Xabi Alonso has a tough task creating unity in such a fragmented squad (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

"You need the right balance of personalities and stages of maturity, with players in their early 20s, early 30s and everything in between," Alonso has said of his squad. Yet the list of new arrivals shows the complicated squad picture the Spaniard has inherited from owners BlueCo:

Geovany Quenda (Sporting CP, undisclosed), Denner (Corinthians, undisclosed), Dastan Satpaev (Kairat Almaty, undisclosed), Emmanuel Emegha (Strasbourg, undisclosed), Marco Palestra (Atalanta, £47m), Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa, £117m), Maxence Lacroix (Crystal Palace, £52m), Danny Welbeck (Brighton, £5m), Jordan Henderson (Brentford, free), Valentin Barco (Strasbourg, undisclosed).

‌



Good luck getting your head around that, Xabi. Oh, and your ranks have been swelled even further by the return from a doping ban of Mykhailo Mudryk, the Ukrainian winger who has not played competitive football since November 2024.

View 4 Images Mykhailo Mudryk has returned to bolster ranks that didn't need bolstering (Image: May JAMES / AFP via Getty Images)

Keeping everyone happy will be an impossible balancing act, given the lack of European football means fewer matches. Perhaps more so than any other elite club, Chelsea is a dog-eat-dog environment where team spirit has been sorely missing in recent years.

Off the pitch there are more factors to try and get your head around. The £10m fine a suspended ban from registering new players for two transfer windows for historic off-the-books agent payments. The fact they are still yet to find a front-of-shirt sponsor, continuing their baffling commercial failure which stretches back to 2023.

‌



Yet, this being the ultimate club of contrasts, they have still splashed out six figures on a top-of-the-range private jet to whisk their players around during pre-season.

Chelsea have 20 days until their begin their Premier League campaign. The size of the task facing Alonso is such that it would be surprising if the picture appeared any clearer by then.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk transfer lined up as club chiefs 'gutted' at missed Liverpool opportunity
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk transfer lined up as club chiefs 'gutted' at missed Liverpool opportunity

An unexpected club has reportedly been planning a move for Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk is being eyed by an MLS club (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

Chicago Fire chiefs were said to be bitterly disappointed by Virgil van Dijk's absence from Liverpool's pre-season tour of America. The MLS club are reportedly lining up a transfer for the defender next summer and were keen to sell themselves to the Reds defender.

‌



The third and final stop of Liverpool's US tour this summer saw them face Leeds United in Chicago, Illinois, where they lost 4-2 on Sunday. Andoni Iraola's side played the match at Soldier Field, the home ground of Chicago Fire, having also used the MLS outfit's performance centre for training sessions.

‌



However, club captain Van Dijk was a notable absentee throughout the entire trip to the States. This was due to Liverpool granting him an extended summer break following his involvement with the Netherlands at the World Cup, meaning he was excused from joining the rest of the squad on tour.

‌

Sports.title: World Cup bombshell as ex-champs 'avoided anti-doping tests' for whole year before winning
Sports.content:
World Cup bombshell as ex-champs 'avoided anti-doping tests' for whole year before winning

Doubt has now emerged on the legitimacy of one World Cup title after shocking claims have emerged

View 2 Images France won their first World Cup title in 1998 (Image: Popperfoto via Getty Images)

The France national team were allegedly exempt from unannounced anti-doping tests for an entire year before winning the World Cup in 1998. That is according to Marie-George Buffet, who served as minister of sports under former Prime Minister Lionel Jospin from 1997 to 2002.

‌



Her revelations have come 13 years after denying such claims in front of a Senate Committee. The politician made the new statement during the documentary 'Zidane: The Making of a Legend', which focuses on the newly-appointed national team boss and his legendary playing career.

‌



However, it was overshadowed by Buffet's admission, which she said was sparked by a surprise anti-doping test during a training camp in Tignes in 1997. The tests were slammed by the players, then-manager Aime Jacquet and the French Football Federation (FFF), who accused the ministry of disrupting their preparations.

‌



All the urine tests had come back negative, but the furious reaction led Buffet to tell Alan Garnier - the doctor who carried out the tests - to no longer bother the team with anti-doping tests, according to Garnier himself.

According to Le Parisien, he said: "I was no longer to bother the French team until the World Cup. In short, no more unannounced tests." The doctor claimed the "verbal directive" was confirmed by Buffet, who acknowledged she faced pressures "of all kinds" when it came to leaving the national team alone.

Arsene Wenger forced to break silence on Gianni Infantino's disastrous World Cup plan READ MORE :

‌



Buffet said on BMFTV: "If Dr Garnier says so, then yes, it must have been true," upon hearing Garnier's remarks. "We didn’t put it quite like that, but it amounts to the same thing. It was a step backwards."

When asked about the origins of the decision to eliminate anti-doping tests for the national team, Buffet responded: "We must have been given instructions at the ministerial level."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan

Gianni Infantino's is under more pressure than ever before and it appears things are only getting harder for the beleaguered FIFA president

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino's position at FIFA may be coming under threat (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Gianni Infantino has been blasted in a leaked email by FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom. The pressure is mounting on the beleaguered FIFA boss, who was forced to ditch his contentious plan to create a commercial subsidiary which can essentially sell stocks in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions.

‌



A furious backlash from the football world forced Infantino into ditching his reviled vision, after UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation publicly revoked his pitch. At the time of writing, the Welsh Football Association, the Swedish FA and the Serbian FA have withdrawn their support for him, with many more tipped to follow suit.

‌



Infantino's grand plan has also been hated from within, as his senior adviser on global strategy and governance Carlos Cordeiro resigned, while Arsene Wenger also publicly stated ditching the vision was "the right thing to do." The anger has not stopped there, as a leaked email from Grafstrom demonstrated.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In an extraordinary message sent to those who work for the governing body of world football, Grafstrom appeared to suggest Infantino's days as the boss of FIFA are numbered.

It read: "A sad and reproachable series of events - which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned - for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

‌



"We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 Member Associations, hand in hand with all relevant stakeholders and in full compliance with the FIFA Statutes and FIFA Regulations.

View 3 Images Grafstrom (right) lashed into Infantino (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

"I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience. You do not need to worry.

‌



"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure.

View 3 Images Infantino seemingly has a mutiny on his hands (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"I also want you to know that my door remains open for you, and I will continue to support our teams, our work and our mission every hour of every day for as long as my work is valued by those we serve."

‌



Grafstrom is the latest senior figure within FIFA to have communicated his anger at the recent drama, either publicly or from within. The pressure looks set to be cranked up on the Swiss football bureaucrat.

UEFA threatened to launch legal action against Infantino's plan, warning him it's "actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints" while also warning him "any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment, or loss of relevant materials following receipt of this notice – or following any earlier date on which you were, or reasonably should have been, aware that proceedings were anticipated – may constitute spoliation of evidence."

Sports.title: Why have Barcelona broken transfer records to sign Kerolin?
Sports.content:
It's been brief. Kerolin only joined the Women's Super League from the NWSL 18 months ago. She now leaves as the English top-flight's most expensive export.

Kerolin's £1.25m fee breaks record held by Olivia Smith's sale from Liverpool to Arsenal last summer. Barcelona were willing to smash their own transfer policy in pursuit of the Brazilian, too, having never previously paid a fee over £500k.

But Kerolin represents an exception to the rule. It's always been that way, from the start of her journey playing barefoot with boys on the streets of Sao Paulo. She was different. The ball hurt to kick, she confessed, but she did it anyway.

Image: Kerolin played a huge part in Man City winning their first WSL title for a decade in 2025-26

As such, there is perhaps an air of inevitability about the 26-year-old's switch to the four-time European champions. This is the path she expected to follow. "Always the most highly-ranked players are playing here or in Spain," she told Sky Sports upon signing for Man City in January 2025. "To be in the vision of the world."

She leaves a WSL champion.

Being considered among the game's most elite does not necessitate playing for Barcelona, but it helps. Each of the last five Ballon d'Or recipients were representing the Catalonia club at the time of winning the prize. Kerolin is now the team-mate of its current holder Aitana Bonmati.

Indeed, if Ballon d'Or is the mission Barcelona has proven the means. It's fertile ground for notoriety and success, with silverware almost guaranteed and the chance to star in a team undergoing reinvention under Pere Romeu. A summer of change has seen plenty of big names leave: Alexia Putellas, Ona Batlle and Mapi Leon among them.

Image: Former Barcelona captain Alexia Putellas is one of three players to join the WSL this summer

But the turning point for Kerolin follows the departure of forward Salma Paralluelo, a player similar in profile to her. The 22-year-old scored twice in last season's Champions League final, a precocious young talent with a huge appetite for success, now clubless after failing to agree terms.

Kerolin, who once held transfer interest from Arsenal, is perfectly poised to succeed her. Barcelona's need for a player of Kerolin's talents is greater than that of City's, flush with versatile wingers, while the considerable fee sends a well-timed message.

Maintenance as Europe's leading superpower does not come cheap. Barcelona have been burdened by financial constraints over the past few years, reliant on their global pull to attract and retain the game's top stars. But others have caught up; no longer is their lure enough in isolation.

To keep pace, Barcelona must show willing to be as financially front-footed as their European rivals. Kerolin's capture is a statement signing for a side in need of some validation after bidding farewell to four high-profile players in as many weeks. Proof that Romeu is remodelling, rather than revolutionising his team of aces.

Nor is this move an ego trip. Kerolin made 26 WSL appearances for Man City, scoring 12 goals. Only Khadija Shaw and Stina Blackstenius have a better goals-per-90 ratio during that time. No player can match Kerolin for take-ons attempted or completed.

In fact, very few forwards boast her complete skillset. She can balance scoring with creating, on-the-ball craft with off-the-ball industry, and has explosive speed in both directions. She scores screamers, too, with quality off both flanks.

Her departure less than two years after signing will feel premature for many in Manchester, not least City's leading scorer Shaw, for whom she made a habit of assisting.
