Sports.title: What happened to Sir Alex Ferguson's trusted lieutenants after Man United's glory years at Old Trafford - as Rene Meulensteen takes up surprise new role at Stockport County
Sports.content:
What happened to Sir Alex Ferguson's trusted lieutenants after Man United's glory years at Old Trafford - as Rene Meulensteen takes up surprise new role at Stockport County

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Rene Meulensteen, Manchester United's former first-team coach who helped Sir Alex Ferguson win seven major trophies during his time at the club, is back in English football after being appointed Stockport County's director of football methodology.

The 62-year-old Dutchman, who was Fulham's head coach for three months during the 2013-14 season, has spent over a decade away from the English game, managing Israel's Maccabi Haifa and India's Kerala Blasters before taking on international coaching roles with Australia and Iraq.

But now, Ferguson's former lieutenant has been tasked with building an 'elite football department' at League One outfit Stockport County, working alongside the club's first-team staff and academy in a surprise new role.

For Red Devils fans, Meulensteen's return is a reminder of the remarkable backroom team Ferguson assembled during his 26-year reign at Old Trafford.

While Sir Alex acted as the figurehead, many of the club's greatest triumphs were built alongside a trusted group of coaches and assistants who mastered tactics, developed promising players and helped maintain the standards that delivered 13 Premier League titles, two Champions Leagues and a myriad of domestic honours.

After Meulensteen's latest career move, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at what Ferguson's trusted right-hand men went on to do after life at Old Trafford.

Rene Meulensteen (right), Man United's former first-team coach who helped Sir Alex Ferguson (left) win seven major trophies during his time at the club, has landed a surprise new role

Meulensteen, pictured in 2008 with Cristiano Ronaldo, has been appointed Stockport County's director of football methodology - in his first role in English football for over a decade

The Dutchman has joined Stockport County in League One as director of football methodology

Carlos Queiroz

The Portuguese, who is widely regarded as Ferguson's most influential assistant, served two spells at Manchester United between 2002-03 and 2004-08, either side of a year as Real Madrid manager.

Queiroz helped modernise United's tactical approach and played a key role in the Red Devils team that won back-to-back Premier League titles and the 2008 Champions League, with Ferguson often crediting him for bringing fresh ideas to Old Trafford.

After leaving Manchester in 2008, Queiroz embarked on a globe-trotting international coaching career, initially managing Portugal at the 2010 World Cup before enjoying two highly successful spells with Iran, leading them to three consecutive World Cups.

One of the most experienced international managers in the game, Queiroz also coached Colombia, Egypt, Qatar and Oman before he was named Ghana head coach ahead of the 2026 World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Taking charge just two months before the tournament, the 73-year-old coach guided the Black Stars to the knockout stages after carving out a goalless draw with England, before losing in the round of 16 against Colombia.

Queiroz is waiting for his next opportunity in football after stepping down following Ghana's World Cup exit.

Carlos Queiroz, who took charge of Ghana at the 2026 World Cup, was Ferguson's trusted No 2

Mike Phelan

Former Manchester United defender Phelan became one of Ferguson's closest confidants during his second spell at Old Trafford, serving as assistant manager from 2008 until the legendary manager's retirement in 2013.

Having first joined the club as a coach in 2001, Phelan was a key figure in the dugout as the Red Devils beefed up their trophy cabinet with five Premier League titles and a Champions League before Ferguson's ultimate farewell.

Following his retirement, Phelan initially stayed on under David Moyes before leaving the club later that year. He went on to manage Hull City during the 2016-17 season but was sacked after just three months with the Tigers rock bottom of the Premier League.

Phelan, who also worked as assistant manager at Central Coast Mariners in Australia, returned to Manchester United in 2018 as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's assistant, steadying the club during the Norwegian's tenure before departing for a second time in 2022.

Since leaving Old Trafford, Phelan has kept a relatively low profile. While he has been linked with several coaching roles, he has instead focused on consultancy work and media appearances, remaining open to a return to management or coaching.

The 63-year-old is currently working as a football consultant and ambassador, with no full-time position in the game.

Mike Phelan, pictured in 2024, is currently working as a football consultant and ambassador

Brian Kidd

Kidd was one of Ferguson's important early lieutenants at United, serving as assistant manager from 1991 to 1998.

A former United player who had been part of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, Kidd returned to Old Trafford after Ferguson's arrival and played a key role in the club's transformation.

He helped oversee the emergence of the Class of '92, including the development of David Beckham, Ryan Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville and the rest of the young squad that became the foundation of United's dominance.

After leaving Old Trafford in 1998, Kidd took his first steps into management with Blackburn Rovers before moving into a series of coaching roles. He worked with Leeds United, England, Sheffield United and Portsmouth, before becoming part of Manchester City's coaching staff in 2009.

As assistant manager under Roberto Mancini and later Manuel Pellegrini, Kidd helped City win two Premier League titles in 2012 and 2014. He stayed at the Etihad for more than a decade and became a rare respected figure across both the blue and red side of Manchester.

Kidd, now 72, left City in 2024 after 15 years at the club and has since stepped away from full-time coaching.

Brian Kidd has stepped away from full-time coaching after fruitful stints at both City and United

Steve McClaren

McClaren's hugely successful spell as Ferguson's No 2 between 1999 and 2001 earned the Englishman his first managerial role at Middlesbrough, where he remained for five years before departing in 2006.

The now 65-year-old boss won the League Cup and reached the 2006 UEFA Cup final with Boro before being appointed England manager, succeeding Sven-Goran Eriksson.

McClaren was sacked 16 months later after he failed to qualify England for the 2008 European Championship and remains to this day the second-shortest serving Three Lions boss in history behind Sam Allardyce, who lasted only 67 days.

Although his spell with the national team ended in disappointment, McClaren rebuilt his reputation by winning the Eredivisie title with FC Twente and later took charge of a host of clubs including Wolfsburg, Nottingham Forest, Derby, Newcastle and Queens Park Rangers.

In 2022, the ex-England boss returned to Manchester United as Erik ten Hag's assistant, before leaving to become Jamaica head coach in 2024.

Steve McClaren was appointed Rotherham United's new head of football back in May

McClaren, like Meulensteen, is now back in English football after being appointed Rotherham United's head of football just three months ago.

The role, which was created after Rotherham suffered relegation to League Two last campaign, will see McClaren provide strategic leadership across the club's football operations, overseeing recruitment and long-term planning.

Archie Knox

Knox, who previously worked with Ferguson at Aberdeen, helped lay the foundations for success at Manchester United between 1986 and 1991, acting as the legendary manager's first true right-hand man at Old Trafford.

The trusted Scot was brought to Manchester to help rebuild the club during what was a difficult transition period under Ferguson, who struggled initially before becoming the most decorated manager in history.

After leaving United in 1991, Knox continued to build an impressive coaching career, following former Rangers and Scotland manager Walter Smith into roles at the Ibrox, Everton and the Scottish national team.

He briefly returned to Aberdeen as assistant manager before enjoying coaching spells at teams including Bolton Wanderers, Blackburn Rovers, Coventry City, Motherwell and Dundee.

Archie Knox, pictured right alongside Ferguson and Gordon Stachan (left) in 2021, has largely stepped away from the public spotlight after retiring from full-time coaching

Knox has since retired from full-time coaching and has largely stepped away from the public spotlight.

Now aged 79, he remains highly respected within Scottish and English football and is remembered as one of Ferguson's most important early allies - the No 2 who helped turn struggling United into a club capable of challenging for major honours.

Eric Harrison

Harrison was never Ferguson's direct No 2, but few people had a greater influence on Manchester United during the club's glory years.

The former Manchester City star joined United as youth team coach in 1981 and remained at the club after Ferguson arrived in 1986, becoming one of the Scot's most trusted figures behind the scenes.

Harrison was tasked with developing United's next generation of players and was the driving force behind the famous Class of '92, nurturing talents including Beckham, Giggs, Scholes, Nicky Butt and the Neville brothers (Gary and Phil). His work provided Ferguson with a core group of players that went on to dominate English football during the 1990s and early 2000s.

Eric Harrison was the driving force behind United's famous Class of '92 (Pictured left to right: Phil Neville, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs, Harrison, Gary Neville, Paul Scholes, David Beckham)

After stepping away from full-time coaching at United in the late 1990s, Harrison continued to have a huge impact on youth development. He worked as a consultant and coach educator, sharing his methods with clubs and coaches, before retiring from football and spending his later years away from the game.

Harrison was diagnosed with dementia and sadly passed away in February 2019 at the age of 81. Ferguson, paying tribute to the immense impact he had on United's golden era, described him as 'one of the greatest coaches of our time'.

Sports.title: New Man City boss Enzo Maresca highlights area of weakness in his squad - as club progress in deal to sign Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi
Sports.content:
New Man City boss Enzo Maresca highlights area of weakness in his squad - as club progress in deal to sign Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Enzo Maresca revealed that Manchester City are looking to land more senior targets this month after losing a wealth of experience over the summer.

Between the departures of Bernardo Silva, John Stones and Nathan Ake, City lost almost 1,000 collective appearances and Maresca appears keen for seasoned additions.

City are progressing in a deal to land Lille’s teenage midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi to supplement the capture of £116million Elliot Anderson as the centre of the park begins to take shape.

Real Madrid are pushing to sign Rodri this summer, with the Spaniard open to a move, and Maresca is acutely aware of the need for older heads to retain balance among the squad.

‘Fortunately this is a squad that doesn’t need to do many things,’ Maresca said. ‘At the same time, as we already know the club lost important players in terms of experience like Bernardo, John and Nathan.’

City have been actively looking at wingers, with a right back having been high on the agenda as well. Maresca is an admirer of Chelsea’s Malo Gusto, with Pedro Neto also linked.

Maresca is acutely aware of the need for older heads to retain balance among the squad

City have been actively looking at wingers, with a right back high on the agenda as well

Director of football Hugo Viana has flown to South Korea for the second leg of City’s tour and is busy juggling a number of different deals, with Tottenham wanting Savinho. Veteran Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is expected to sign once James Trafford’s switch to Leeds United is finalised.

‘Hugo is here, also (chief executive) Ferran (Soriano) is here and we just try to speak day by day to see if we need to do something,’ Maresca added.

‘For sure, there are things that we need to do. We are in communication every day. The transfer window is open and when it’s open anything can happen.’

At 26, Phil Foden is one of the club’s senior stars now and has raised his hand to be included in the captaincy group.

Foden wore the armband for the weekend draw with Inter in Hong Kong. City generally operate with a four or five-man captaincy group, usually ratified after the transfer window closes.

‘I have to be really,’ Foden said when asked if he will be considered a leader. ‘I’ve been at the club for so long, I’m one of the longest here.

‘So this season I have to be one of the leaders, one of the captains. I’m looking forward to that new responsibility and trying to take leadership.’

Meanwhile, City’s friendly with the K-League All Stars is set to be staged amid a local government warning of excessive heat.

Players were greeted in South Korea by an emergency alert on their smartphones, issued when temperatures are forecast to reach 38C or higher.

Sports.title: 'I still miss him': EFL manager opens up for first time on tragic death of Mark Hughes' son Alex at age of 38
Sports.content:
Grimsby Town head coach David Artell has opened up on the tragic sudden death of Alex Hughes - son of Manchester United legend Mark - following his passing in June.

Hughes, 38, worked as player recruitment lead at the League Two side, with his shock passing leaving an enormous loss among players and staff in Lincolnshire.

Speaking to BBC Humberside, Artell appeared close to tears as he shared a poignant tribute to his late colleague.

'He was a lovely guy, top guy. He was good at his job, very humble,' Artell said.

'In those kind of roles, (people) tend to have a high opinion of themselves, rightly or wrongly. I'm not saying that for every kind of head of recruitment, but they tend to really back their own judgement. He was really happy to listen to everyone in the room.

'Life can be really cruel. He's a good guy.

David Artell talked for the first time about the death of, player recruitment lead, Alex Hughes. #gtfc @jameshoggarth @officialgtfc



Listen to the full interview here: https://t.co/8631Xt7fmL pic.twitter.com/M853ZyPqit — BBC Humberside Sport (@HumbersideSport) August 4, 2026

Grimsby Town manager David Artell has opened up on his grief following the shock death of player recruitment lead Alex Hughes (right)

Hughes' funeral last month saw hundred of mourners pay tribute to the son of the Man United legend after his sudden death

'It's not easy,' Artell admitted when asked how he was feeling, and the impact of his grief in recent weeks. 'It's not easy. You have to pull your big boy pants on and get on with it.

'You have to understand that whatever I'm feeling, the family's going through it 1000 times worse.

'I still miss him, obviously. It's just sad. Really sad.'

Sir Alex Ferguson was among the hundreds of mourners who turned out for Hughes' funeral in Prestbury last month, alongside other former Man United figures such as Mike Phelan, Martin Edwards, Bryan Robson and Ryan Giggs.

The League Managers Association (LMA) had announced Alex's death in June, releasing a statement on behalf of former Man City and Wales boss Hughes.

'Jill and I are totally heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected loss of our beloved son Alex,' the statement read.

'Alex was a wonderful son, brother to Curtis and Xenna, devoted husband and father to Jessica and their two beautiful children Sebastian and Leonardo.

'Alex was Player Recruitment Lead at Grimsby Town FC, and had many good friends and colleagues. He will be so deeply missed by us all.

'We ask for privacy during this sad time as we come to terms with our family's loss. The Hughes family.'

After a brief playing career in Wales, Hughes became a licensed agent, and went on to work with his father as an analyst at clubs he managed including Blackburn Rovers, Manchester City and Fulham.

Hughes later served as director of football at AFC Fylde before joining Grimsby Town.

Sports.title: Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow
Sports.content:
Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow

Commonwealth Cup winner Venetian Sun has been ruled out for the rest of the season after trainer Karl Burke confirmed the sprinter has suffered a tendon injury

View 3 Images Tony Bloom (second left) with Venetian Sun, who followed up her success at Royal Ascot with a Group 1 victory in France (Image: PA)

Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine Venetian Sun has suffered an injury setback that will sideline her for the remainder of the campaign.

‌



Among last year's top juveniles, the lightning-quick daughter of Starman – owned by Brighton & Hove Albion chairman in partnership with Ian McAleavy – has maintained her brilliant form this season, claiming a second Royal Ascot triumph when storming to Commonwealth Cup glory.

‌



Her most recent outing saw her produce an excellent runner-up effort against older rivals at Newmarket in the July Cup, and she had been under consideration for a trip to France for this weekend's Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville, the venue where she captured the Prix Morny as a two-year-old.

‌



Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing READ MORE :

Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot READ MORE :

Nevertheless, plans for the remainder of her three year old campaign have been shelved following the discovery of a tendon problem.

Her trainer Karl Burke said: "It's a big shame and unfortunately it happens. It's a long way from being a career- or life-threatening injury, but obviously is going to take time and it's very disappointing.

"We had more or less decided to swerve Deauville anyway because the ground was very fast out there last weekend with no sign of any rain and the French not watering like they used to do.

‌



View 3 Images Celebrations on the track after Venetian Sun's Royal Ascot victory (Image: Getty Images)

"It's just one of those things, we have a feeling she may have initiated it at Newmarket during the July Cup but she came back from there with a nasty little cut and she had been on antibiotics and anti-inflammatories and we think that may have masked it to a degree."

Venetian Sun has triumphed in six of her nine career starts to date, with her connections eagerly anticipating an autumn schedule that could have featured appearances in Haydock's Sprint Cup, at Ascot on British Champions Day and at the Breeders' Cup.

‌



Explaining the setback, Burke added: "It's basically a strain to the tendon, it happens a lot with jumping horses – it's unusual really at this stage in a sprinter's life, but can happen.

View 3 Images Venetian Sun sprinted to victory at Ascot (Image: Martin Dokoupil/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

"It's a time thing now and she will have the next six or seven months on the easy list and then be reassessed from there.

Article continues below

"The little bit of work she has done the last few days has just aggravated it and we've had the vets in this morning and they weren't 100 per cent happy with a little bit of heat in the leg and that is what it turns out to be.

"The plan before today was if she finished the season in good shape she would stay in training and that may still be the plan, but that is a discussion for later on."

Sports.title: Man Utd exploit Premier League loophole to announce world-leading £20m deal
Sports.content:
Man Utd exploit Premier League loophole to announce world-leading £20m deal

Manchester United have announced a substantial new sponsorship deal with Betway ahead of the 2026/27 season, when gambling companies will be banned from the front of shirts

View 3 Images Manchester United have struck a £20m-per-season deal with Betway (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have struck a multi-year sponsorship deal worth £20million per season with Betway. The gambling company will be visible on United's training kit and around Old Trafford on matchdays as part of the deal, which covers the men's and women's teams.

‌



The Premier League giants went the 2025/26 campaign without a training kit sponsor and are delighted to have changed that ahead of the new season kicking off. Despite being worth less than their previous deal with blockchain company Tezos, which brought in £24m-a-season, United are delighted with a deal bigger than any other standalone training kit or playing shirt sleeve deals in world football.

‌



Marc Armstrong, chief business officer at United, said: "The scale of our exciting new partnership reflects our growth strategy, the enduring global strength and appeal of Manchester United, and our ability to attract leading brands that want to engage with our vast worldwide fanbase."

‌



The sponsorship will run alongside United's £60m-a-season sponsorship deal with electronics company Snapdragon, who will continue to be displayed on the front of their shirts.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

7 Man Utd players face uncertain futures as part of huge summer overhaul of squad READ MORE :

The 2026/27 Premier League season is the first in which gambling companies are not allowed on the front of shirts. Premier League clubs agreed to get rid of gambling companies back in April 2023 and the rule has now come into effect.

‌



However, although gambling companies are gone from the front of shirts, they are still allowed on the sleeves and training kits, as well as being plastered all over stadiums via advertising hoardings.

It is a loophole that campaigners warned the Premier League about last year after research showed how teams in foreign leagues that had implemented a similar gambling ban easily found ways around it.

View 3 Images Betway will be visible on Manchester United's training kit (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



As Nick Harvey from the Coalition to End Gambling Ads (CEGA) told Mirror Football: “With tens of thousands of ads still plastered across stadiums, shirt sleeves and the media, removing shirt-front logos is already just a gesture."

While six top-flight clubs have been able to swap out their previous gambling deals for non-gambling front-of-shirt sponsors, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland are currently set to begin the campaign without a sponsor, having been unable to strike a deal. Meanwhile, Chelsea are also sponsor-less after their short-term deal with AI company IFS expired.

Although United are yet to find a sleeve sponsor for the upcoming season, they are right to flag their "enduring global appeal". Manchester Evening News reports that United held off agreeing deals with other companies in order to wait for a better one with Betway.

‌



View 3 Images Snapdragon are still Manchester United's front-of-shirt sponsor (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

Sean Connell, editor of The Sponsor, an independent sponsorship research and valuation publication, recently told Mirror Football about the widening gap between the 'Big Six' Premier League sides and the rest when it comes to sponsorship.

"The gambling ban has taken what was already a shrinking pool of sponsors and removed a healthy chunk of those," Connell said. "It’s created what I believe is the most competitive and difficult sponsorship environment that Premier League clubs have ever faced."

‌



Before the ban, Gambling companies had been willing to pay mid-table Premier League sides twice what other companies offered for sponsorship deals. It means that many clubs have been forced to shake hands on sponsorships worth considerably less this season.

Betway have become United's 'principle partner' but are also betting partners of Arsenal, Manchester City, Chelsea, Brighton, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Fulham in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Dominik Szoboszlai explains Liverpool post-match 'spat' and change players will make
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai explains Liverpool post-match 'spat' and change players will make

Dominik Szoboszlai has poured water on any possible spat with Curtis Jones after the pair were seen having a heated conversation after a Liverpool pre-season outing

View 2 Images Dominik Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones were seen clashing after Liverpool's game last week

Liverpool star Dominik Szoboszlai has cleared up any talk of a bust up with Curtis Jones - but admitted that frank discussions should take place in the changing room, rather than on the pitch

‌



‌



The pair were seen clashing following the win over Wrexham in New York last week. The academy graduate was visibly frustrated at full-time and was seen having words with Szoboszlai and Kostas Tsimikas.

‌



The issue reportedly came about after Tsimikas was given given the armband once Szoboszlai came off in second-half and videos of the discussion went viral on social media, forcing the Hungarian to address the situation.

Szoboszlai has played down the magnitude of the incident but maintained he would love to step up into a leadership role following Andy Robertson's exit - leaving the vice captaincy absent.

He said: "It was never a debate between us three. We just discussed something on the pitch. What (which) actually after you guys make it very big.

‌



Liverpool set for major cash injection as club enter advanced talks after £324m reveal READ MORE :

4 transfers Liverpool need to complete after Leeds defeat showed harsh reality READ MORE :

"But next time we will manage to do it in the changing room. But no, nobody was angry at no one. It's all cleared. We are cool, everybody. No, there hasn't been any conversation [about the vice captaincy]. Obviously we have Virgil as the captain.

"We have Alisson. We have Joe Gomez. So there was no conversation at all. Obviously Ali is not here. Joe is injured. I was very proud moment to have it. And let's see. It's not my choice. It's not fixed. If you get offered the vice-captain in Liverpool FC, you're going to take it. It would be a proud moment for me. But I respect everybody."

View 2 Images The Hungarian had been wearing the armband and is keen for a leadership role

‌



Liverpool have maintained that clashes like that are part of an elite environment and Szoboszlai and Jones have since been seen laughing together at an opening training session in Chicago.

Jones has just under a year remaining on his contract at Anfield and Liverpool are naturally trying to avoid losing him on a free transfer. Inter Milan have made repeated attempts to try and sign the versatile Reds star but have now seen three bids turned down.

The Premier League side are sticking to their valuation, which is a minimum of £35million. The Reds were dealt a reality check in the US when they blew a lead to lose 4-2 to Leeds as Andoni Iraola continues his push for more new signings.

Sports.title: Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing
Sports.content:
Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing

The top jockey received the hefty sentence by Sandown stewards for easing up on a horse who was subsequently beaten by a nose last month

View 3 Images Thunder Home (far side) is caught on the line by Zero Error (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

Rossa Ryan won a partial victory against a massive 28-day riding ban at an appeal hearing on Tuesday.

‌



The 26-year-old rider, who is in third place in the Flat jockeys championship behind Billy Loughnane and Oisin Murphy, was found guilty of ‘failing to take all reasonable and permissible measures to obtain the best possible placing on a horse that would have finished first’ when he rode Thunder Home, who finished second in a race at Sandown last month.

‌



The James Horton-trained runner had led nearly all the way until he was caught right on the line by the fast-finishing Zero Error who won by a nose under Jamie Spencer.

‌



Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot READ MORE :

At an appeal before a BHA disciplinary panel, BHA regulatory counsel Catherine Daly said Ryan’s mount had been four lengths clear with half a furlong of the 7f race to run but the jockey then “places both his hands back on the reins” and then “can be clearly seen to stop riding with said vigour” for about three strides, or one second.

“It is my case that this horse clearly would have won this race had Mr Ryan not eased off,” he said. “It’s not a matter of ‘could’ have won.”

In his evidence Ryan described Thunder Home as an inexperienced two-year-old who had “worked incredibly hard” to establish his advantage.

‌



View 3 Images Rossa Ryan: had his ban reduced to ten days (Image: PA)

“I put my stick down because the horse has given me everything,” he said. “When I put my stick down my horse’s speed is decreasing. His stride isn’t but his speed is. I am really starting to feel the hill in Sandown.

“He’s been alone in front from the get-go. Late on he has changed his legs to try and stretch again and he can’t. What the BHA argue I don’t agree with. I’m actually adjusting my body.. I have never stopped riding my mount.”

‌



He later added: “I think Mr Spencer would have won either way.”

During cross-examination Daly quoted the Sandown inquiry transcript in which Ryan had admitted he ‘thought he had the race won’ and that he expected Thunder Home to ‘coast to the line, not a problem. There is one stride I missed where you can make an argument that I didn’t fully extend my hands’.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Daly asked: “Did you ease off and stop applying the same pressure because you expected he’d coast to the line?”

Ryan said: “I didn’t ease off. I adjusted what I’d seen fit to the horse on the day. When I emphasise ‘coast’ I mean as in he doesn’t need the stick. He’s given me everything.”

He admitted not knowing Spencer was closing. Daly asedk: “If you had realised Mr Spencer was there you would have kept riding with the same vigour that you had been riding and your horse would have won the race, wouldn’t it?” “No.” said Ryan.

‌



Ryan’s solicitor Rory Mac Neice said: “Keeping a horse in balance is imperative. This horse is a two-year-old. It was the first time in its life it had been in front for the whole race. It was tiring. It shifts left at the very point we see the alteration in Mr Ryan’s riding. The horse then changed its lead which allows the horse to flatten and Mr Ryan immediately flattens with it.

“That adjustment is reasonable in the circumstances of this race and the horse he is riding.”

View 3 Images Jockey Jamie Spencer: rider of winner Zero Error

‌



Panel chair HH James O'Mahony said the BHA had presented “a classic case of a jockey easing down when he thought he had the race won”, adding, “And he hadn't realised that with a typical, perhaps, Jamie Spencer, run, if I may be permitted to say that, he was coming with great knots on his outside to, as it were, nick the race.”

Ryan’s case was that he adjusted his riding “by moving his body weight to the rhythm of the horse in circumstances where the horse was declining in strength and impetus at that stage of the race, and that that was a perfectly proper thing for a jockey to do”.

He added: “On the balance of probabilities, we prefer the BHA account, and we conclude that it is the correct account.”

Article continues below

However the panel ruled that this race was one Ryan “could, and not would” have won. ”And in those circumstances, it's not compulsory to impose a sanction of 28 days. The appropriate figure is one of 10 days.”

The ban will begin on August 6.

Sports.title: Tottenham offered chance to sign ex-Arsenal striker Folarin Balogun after World Cup storm
Sports.content:
Tottenham offered chance to sign ex-Arsenal striker Folarin Balogun after World Cup storm

Tottenham have been offered the opportunity to strengthen their strike force in the transfer market as Roberto De Zerbi continues to improve his squad

View 2 Images Folarin Balogun could be on the move (Image: Roy Rochlin/Getty Images for Fanatics)

Tottenham have been offered United States international Folarin Balogun. The striker's representatives are said to have reached out to Spurs directly with a proposal for the former Arsenal youngster.

‌



Balogun, who was at the centre of a FIFA World Cup scandal after his red-card punishment was suspended following communication between US President Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino, is said to be available for a 'competitive fee'.

‌



The Monaco forward has an uncertain role in the Ligue 1 side's long-term plans, and his availability makes him an attractive option following the intermediaries' approach, per the Sun. A deal would still require Monaco to do business for the 25-year-old who scored 19 goals in 43 matches for Les Monegasques.

‌



Balogun joined the Principality club in 2023, having come through the youth ranks at Arsenal. If Tottenham were to agree a deal with Monaco, they would face their north London rivals benefiting from a 17.5% sell-on clause.

The goalscorer looked set to be one of the stars of the World Cup in the United States after bagging three goals in four World Cup matches. His efforts were overshadowed by the controversy surrounding his sending off during the competition.

Arsene Wenger forced to break silence on Gianni Infantino's disastrous World Cup plan READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino pushed to quit FIFA and Donald Trump stance as nations rally against him READ MORE :

Balogun was sent off in the round of 32 against Bosnia and Herzegovina after accidentally hitting the back of Tarik Muharemovic's leg with his studs. It was only after VAR intervened that Balogun was given his marching orders, but the drama did not end there.

‌



The forward was permitted to play in the next round against Belgium when his expected ban was suspended for a year. The move came after pressure was piled on from the host nation, including from Trump and his administration.

While Balogun's inclusion could not prevent the United States from crashing out of the tournament, the decision came in for some severe criticism. "I think it's an absolute disgrace, I really do," said Wayne Rooney on punditry duty for the BBC.

View 2 Images Balogun was sent off for this tackle (Image: AP Photo/Jeff Chiu)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"I know it's UEFA but I got a three-game ban before Euro 2012. I was due to miss the three group games and I got told if I went over to Switzerland and did a training session with a bunch of kids, my third game would get taken off. I agreed to do it because I didn't want a three-game ban but I thought that was wrong.

"For this to be suspended, they either take the red card away, which is probably the right decision, and then he can play. But to suspend it for a year? I think it's an absolute disgrace. Infantino should be ashamed of this.

‌



"The sportsmanship of this game is in question here. If I'm USA's opponent, I'd be absolutely fuming. It's wrong in every way. If you're an England player tonight or a Mexican player, and you get a red card, do you expect to be playing the next game? Where does it stop?"

Posting after the tournament, Balogun reflected on his nation's campaign and apologised to fans in the United States. He was not drawn on the controversy he had been embroiled in, however.

He wrote: "My debut World Cup...It hurts to wait 4 years to compete at the highest level our sport has to offer. I want to say sorry to our fans it was not good enough when it mattered most and we let you down.

Article continues below

"Soccer in America will only become bigger the belief, the talent, and the passion is continually growing and I know the best days are in front of us, the future belongs to those who never stop believing, this moment will fuel us. We will be back. Why not us? For the nation. For the flag."

Sports.title: Team GB hero holds back tears in passionate BBC Breakfast plea to Andy Burnham
Sports.content:
Team GB hero holds back tears in passionate BBC Breakfast plea to Andy Burnham

A Team GB hero broke down in tears on BBC Breakfast while speaking directly to Andy Burnham

View 2 Images Archie Goodburn sent an emotional appeal to Prime Minister Andy Burnham (Image: BBC Breakfast)

Commonwealth Games star Archie Goodburn was moved to tears live on BBC Breakfast as he made a heartfelt plea to Prime Minister Andy Burnham to pour more funding and resources into brain cancer research. The swimmer, 25, was diagnosed with a rare inoperable cancer just over two years ago after doctors discovered a number of oligodendrogliomas on his brain.

‌



The condition is terminal and he may never reach his 40s. Yet, that has done nothing to dampen Goodburn's determination to pursue his ambitions while continuing to passionately raise awareness. He's represented Great Britain internationally and was one of the major talking points of the Commonwealth Games.

‌



The Scot took part in the 50m breaststroke final last week, finishing seventh. He was hailed as an inspiration by fellow racers and appeared on BBC Breakfast just days later.

‌



On Tuesday morning, he spoke about the new Rare Cancers Bill and delivered an emotional message to newly-appointed PM Burnham, calling for greater investment in advancing cancer treatment across the UK.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Josh Kerr sends clear message after being left hurt by BBC SPOTY snub READ MORE :

Goodburn began to well up and tremble as he asked which camera was broadcasting live, before staring directly down the lens and making a personal appeal to Downing Street to help alleviate the "unbearable" suffering endured by brain cancer patients and their loved ones.

‌



He said: "So Andy Burnham, if you believe and you want to make a change and a difference to the future of our country and our young population, please listen to us. Please establish a national brain cancer lead and give us a chance to fight for our lives because honestly, the things that patients are going through out there is just unbelievable and so unjust.

"There are clinical trials around the world, in the US, in Australia, in China, that could change lives, and we are not seeing them in the UK, and it is unfair and unjust. So please, please invest and make the difference because I'm on my knees begging for not just my own life but those of my best friends and those who are affected and the families all around the country.

View 2 Images The Scot competed in the 50m breaststroke final last week (Image: Ian MacNicol, Getty Images)

‌



"This has to change. It's been going on for too long and the suffering is unbearable. I'm sorry. The Rare Cancers Bill is not going to be enough. It is a step in the right direction, but it is not going to cover, it's not going to make the changes we need."

In recent years, ground-breaking treatments have emerged with the capacity to save lives. Most significant in Goodburn's situation was Vorasidenib, a breakthrough treatment which enabled him to postpone the possibility of chemotherapy and fulfil his ambitions of racing in the pool.

Goodburn had started off by saying: "What's frustrating, and we welcome the Rare Cancers Bill, but that Rare Cancers Bill we truly do not believe is going to be enough to make the changes.

Article continues below

"The Rare Cancers Bill covers 14 different types of cancers, rare cancers. Brain cancer is one of these in terms of incidents of diagnosis, but it's not the same in terms of the number of deaths it causes. It is extremely deadly.

"Yes, it's rare, but it's extremely deadly. This frustrates me immensely. And the Rare Cancers Bill establishes two new positions, a clinical lead and a research lead. These two roles are part-time across 14 different types of cancers, and they accumulate to 36 days a year.

"Those two roles to cover 14 different types of cancers to try and change the landscape of treatment. I do not see how 36 days a year is going to make that change for 14 different types of cancers, let alone the most deadly type of cancer."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
