World.title: The Dangerous Return of PF Staged Political Violence
World.content:
By Michael Lombe

Zambia has been here before. And we must not go back. The Patriotic Front has a documented history of manufacturing crises to play the victim and stoke division. The most notorious chapter came under Mr Steven Kampyongo as Minister of Home Affairs, but the script was written earlier.

Under the late President Michael Sata, the PF conjured an imaginary group called “Tonga under Oaths”. The then Lusaka Province Police Commissioner, Ms Charity Katanga, was deployed to give it weight. The claim was grotesque: that the group had killed a Bemba child in Mazabuka and was ordering all Bemba people out of Southern Province.

President Sata saw through it. While swearing in Mr Wynter Kabimba as Justice Minister, he dismissed the tale outright. Turning to the then Defence Minister, Mr Geoffrey Bwalya Mwamba, one of the architects of the plot, he said the idea was fake and must be dropped immediately before it caused war.

The PF did not stop. Next came the story that Bemba fishermen were being chased off the Kafue River. The Disaster Management and Mitigation Unit delivered tents to “displaced” people who did not exist. The lie collapsed.

Then came the market fires and the gassings. Hundreds died including schoolchildren. Paid voices were lined up to blame the then opposition leader, Mr Hakainde Hichilema and the UPND. That too failed, because Zambians refused to be baited.

Now, in opposition, the PF and its Tonse Alliance appear to be dusting off the same playbook.

Leaked reports reveals a plan to stage attacks on their own campaign teams as they tour Southern Province. Recruits, it is said will be hired, masked, and instructed to stone their own vehicles in Monze, Choma and Kalomo. Media teams will be on standby. The purpose is clear: run back to Eastern and Northern provinces with video and say, “This is what Southerners are doing to us.”

If these allegations are true, they are not politics. They are sabotage.

This is the politics of arson, not argument. It seeks power not through policy, but through fear, tribal baiting, and staged blood.

Zambians rejected this in 2016. They rejected it in 2021. They will reject it again in 2026.

We owe it to the market traders, the schoolchildren, and the farmers who paid the price last time to say it plainly: do not light this country on fire for votes.

The law must act. The public must watch. And the media must not be used as a prop in a staged drama.

The past has instructed us. Let us not repeat it.

World.title: UN unveils 2025 Annual Results Report
World.content:
The United Nations in Zambia has unveiled its 2025 Annual Results Report, highlighting the impact of coordinated partnerships in advancing national development and improving the lives of vulnerable communities across the country.

Launching the report during a media breakfast in Lusaka this morning, United Nations Resident Coordinator, Beatrice Mutali, said the report demonstrates that sustainable development can only be achieved through strong collaboration among government, development partners, civil society, the private sector, communities and the media.

Ms Mutali added that the document showcases the collective achievements made in key sectors such as health, education, women’s and youth empowerment, climate resilience, food security and the attainment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

She stressed that the report is not merely a record of the United Nations’ work, but a reflection of the results achieved through partnerships that support Zambia’s national development priorities, while ensuring that no one is left behind.

The UN Resident Coordinator explained that this was the first time the organisation had presented its Annual Results Report directly to journalists, describing the move as an important step towards strengthening transparency and public understanding of the organisation’s contribution to Zambia’s development agenda.

She noted that the media remains a strategic partner in communicating development outcomes, amplifying community voices and helping citizens understand how policies and programmes translate into tangible benefits.

“This report reflects what we can achieve when we work together towards a common goal of sustainable development,” Ms Muntali said.

Ms Muntali, who is also preparing to conclude her tenure as United Nations Resident Coordinator later this month, said serving in Zambia has been a privilege, citing the resilience and determination of the Zambian people as a source of inspiration.

She expressed confidence that the strong partnership between the United Nations and the Zambian media will continue to promote awareness of development efforts and support the country’s journey towards inclusive and sustainable development.

Presenting one of the pillars in the report on prosperity, during the UN Media Breakfast, Food and Agriculture Organisation Projects Coordinator, Esther Chingoma, said the pillar focuses on enabling people, particularly the poor, vulnerable and marginalised, to pursue sustainable livelihoods, decent employment and entrepreneurship.

Ms Chingoma said one of the major achievements recorded in 2025 was the strengthening of skills development through the launch of the Mining Sector Skills Committee, which has enhanced coordination between industry and skills development institutions.

She added that skills planning was also strengthened through reviews in the agriculture and tourism sectors, while recommendations were developed to improve the financing and effectiveness of skills development programmes.

Ms Chingoma disclosed that 32,100 smallholder farmers and 195 Ministry of Agriculture staff were trained in climate-smart and regenerative agricultural practices to improve food security and resilience.

“Our goal is to ensure that vulnerable communities have the skills, opportunities and resilience needed to build sustainable livelihoods,” Ms Chingoma said.

World.title: Police records reduction in stolen property during this year’s agriculture show
World.content:
Zambia Police Spokesperson, Godfrey Chilabi, has disclosed that property valued at K183, 950 was reported stolen during the just ended 98th Zambia Agricultural and Commercial Show, compared to last year’s property which was valued at K339, 590.

Mr Chilabi has also confirmed to the media in Lusaka that a total of 32 criminal cases and one Road Traffic Accident were recorded at the Lusaka Showgrounds, between July 29th and August 3rd, 2026.

He has described this as a significant reduction from 65 criminal cases reported last year, representing a 50.8 percent drop.

Mr Chilabi attributed the improvement to enhanced security measures put in place by the Zambia Police in partnership with other security agencies as well as increased security consciousness among show-goers.

“The Service also commends police officers and other security personnel for their commitment and dedication towards ensuring public safety and security throughout the show,” Mr Chilabi stated.

According to Mr Chilabi, the majority of cases involved theft from persons, with 21 incidents mainly targeting mobile phones with six other thefts including laptops, groceries, and personal property.

He disclosed that Police have since arrested 12 suspects in connection with various offences, notable among them, a suspect found tampering with a parked motor vehicle where officers recovered a break-in instrument believed to have been used in the crime.

Mr Chilabi stated that the suspects remain in custody as investigations continue, further assuring that operations are underway to recover more stolen property.

He noted that additional reports included one case of theft by servant involving 13 tins of shoe polish valued at K990, three cases of Assault Occasioning Actual Bodily Harm, and one case of tampering with a motor vehicle and malicious damage.

Mr Chilabi also revealed that nineteen mobile phones were stolen during the show, with Sunday recording the highest number at 10, while stolen items included six handbags, three laptops, groceries, cash, and personal documents.

The Police Spokesperson has further urged members of the public to remain vigilant in crowded places, secure their valuables, and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest police officer.

World.title: Judiciary ready to handle August election disputes – Dr Malila
World.content:
Chief Justice Mumba Malila, says the Judiciary is fully prepared to determine all election-related disputes independently, professionally and within the timelines prescribed by the law in the August 13 General Elections.

Speaking when he officially opened the Electoral Dispute Resolution Training Programme in Lusaka today, Dr Malila said the training marks the culmination of a three-year institutional programme aimed at strengthening the Judiciary’s capacity to administer electoral justice.

“The Judiciary shall not choose elections, neither does it determine political outcomes. These choices belong to the people of Zambia. Our constitutional responsibility begins when disputes arise,” Dr Malila said.

The Chief Justice noted that recent constitutional and electoral reforms, including the increase in parliamentary constituencies and the introduction of the mixed member proportional representation system, are expected to increase the volume and complexity of election petitions, making judicial preparedness critical.

“No one, not even the Chief Justice, will direct you on how to decide your case. Look at the facts, look at the law and consider your conscience before making your determination,” he told judges, magistrates and tribunal members.

Meanwhile, Chairperson of the Chief Justice’s Advisory Committee on Election Management, Maria Kawimbe, stated that the Judiciary has undertaken nationwide specialised training for judges, magistrates, research advocates, legal practitioners and court staff to ensure they are fully prepared to adjudicate electoral disputes.

Justice Kawimbe said by the end of the programme, the committee would have trained 117 magistrates, 69 research advocates, 147 court support staff and about 230 legal practitioners expected to serve on Local Government Election Tribunals.

“Election petitions are governed by strict, non-negotiable timelines that leave no room to learn procedure as a matter proceeds,” Justice Kawimbe said.

And Commonwealth Secretariat Director for Governance and Peace, Elizabeth Macharia, stated that credible elections depend on strong institutions capable of resolving disputes fairly and impartially.

“The courts do not replace the will of the people but help ensure that the will of the people is expressed, protected and respected within the framework of the law,” Dr Macharia said.

Earlier, Chairperson of the Chief Justice Advisory Committee on Training and Continuing Education, Justice Pixie Yangailo, said the programme is designed to strengthen institutional preparedness by equipping adjudicators and court staff with the knowledge and skills required to administer electoral justice consistently and efficiently.

Also speaking at the same programme, Chandler Institute of Justice Operations Director, Waicha Ndlovu, said a Judiciary that resolves electoral disputes professionally and within the law is essential for sustaining public confidence in democratic institutions.

Ms Ndlovu added that the institute remains committed to supporting judicial capacity building in Zambia.

World.title: Samfya’s US$1 million Aquaculture Park operational
World.content:
Government has operationalised the US$1 Million Samfya Aquaculture Park, a major investment designed to transform fish farming in Luapula Province and expand opportunities for communities living around Lake Bangweulu.

Ministry of Information and Media Director Spokesperson, Henry Kapata, said during his recent visit to the province that President Hakainde Hichilema indicated that the waters of Lake Bangweulu must benefit the people who live around them, adding that the facility is part of that vision.

Mr Kapata says the Aquaculture Park is expected to produce one million fish fingerlings every year, train fish farmers, fabricate fish cages locally and support the expansion of commercial aquaculture across Samfya, Chifunabuli and neighbouring districts.

He stated that the government has already empowered cooperatives with fish cages on Lake Bangweulu, helping communities move beyond capture fishing towards sustainable fish farming that creates jobs, increases incomes and protects fish stocks for future generations.

Mr Kapata has told the media that the facility forms part of the broader US$50.89 Million Zambia Aquaculture Enterprise Development Project, supported by the African Development Bank and the Zambian government, aimed at unlocking Luapula’s fisheries and aquaculture potential.

He further said from producing fingerlings to supporting fish farmers and strengthening the entire fisheries value chain, the investment positions Samfya as one of Zambia’s emerging aquaculture hubs.

World.title: Kabompo district receives ballot papers
World.content:
Stakeholders in Kabompo District of Northwestern Province have commended the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) for the transparency in the delivery of ballot papers for the August 13, 2026 General Elections.

Speaking after witnessing the arrival of ballot papers for Kabompo East and West Constituencies yesterday, United Party for National Development (UPND) District Chairlady, Grace Mazaka, says the arrival of ballot paper in the district is a relief to political parties and other stakeholders that are participating in this year’s election.

“The long-awaited moment has finally arrived, the upcoming election day is important to us as a party,” she said.

Ms Mazaka dismissed allegations of malpractice circulating in some quarters, stating that ballot papers and boxes remained fully intact.

“We have all witnessed the arrival of the ballots papers for the two constituencies and ballot papers are intact and sealed and we want to remind other political parties to take note that the UPND does not get involved in any electoral malpractice,” she said.

Independent Aspiring Candidates Representative, David Kapwepwe, described the process as transparent.

“The ballot materials were received, verified, and documented upon arrival and serial numbers were recorded and photographed and all materials were signed with no signs of tampering,” he said.

Meanwhile, Kabompo West Returning Officer, Costa Namakando, said the ballot papers are secured with 24hours security from the police.

World.title: Constitutional Court urged to revisit running mate ruling before crisis deepens
World.content:
Constitutional Court ruling on running mates risks legal quagmire, lawyer warns

A recent Constitutional Court decision holding that running mates are not candidates has pushed the court itself into an awkward legal position, constitutional lawyer Dr Joseph Chirwa has warned, cautioning that the ruling could create a constitutional crisis unless revisited.

In a statement, Chirwa said the holding places the Constitutional Court in a quagmire it put itself in and will struggle to escape, comparing the situation to an earlier judgment, Michelo Chizombe v Edgar Chagwa Lungu, which he said was decided per incuriam, meaning without proper regard to relevant law.

The commentary follows a case brought by activist Isaac Mwanza, who approached the court seeking a legal interpretation on independent candidates and running mate withdrawal. Chirwa said the ruling had, in effect, put the Constitutional Court itself on trial.

“The Constitutional Court, which has ruled repeatedly that the Constitution is to be read in a manner that promotes the Bill of Rights as provided under Article 267, has effectively killed other fundamental freedoms and rights under Article 19 [freedom of conscience] and Article 21 [freedom of assembly and association] as read with Article 11(b) of Act No. 18 of 1996,” Chirwa said.

He argued that the constitutional provisions in question give a person the right to change their mind and choose who to associate and assemble with, and that requiring a person to remain tied to a previous decision, even when they no longer support it, creates unintended consequences for those freedoms.

“How can a constitution be interpreted to give effect to the Bill of Rights when some freedoms and rights are being unintentionally sacrificed and killed?” Chirwa asked.

He urged the Constitutional Court to revisit its ruling before it creates a broader constitutional crisis, outlining what he described as an unworkable contradiction at the heart of the current position. The court, he said, has simultaneously held that running mates are not candidates while also treating a presidential candidate and running mate as a twinned, paired unit that cannot exist independently of one another.

“How can you have twins who are not twins? How can you have a pair which is not a pair?” he said. “By implication, whether or not the Constitution expressly refers to running mates as candidates, a running mate is a candidate for the election of vice president.”

Chirwa said a resignation from a political party, or a withdrawal from the race, should render a twinned ticket incompetent and its nomination invalid, arguing that forcing a person to remain part of a ticket they no longer wish to be associated with amounts to a denial of their right to freely associate.

“You cannot force one to be part of a ticket and deny him or her the right to associate or assemble. To force a person to run for an election which they don’t want to be a part of, as they may have changed their mind, is unconscionable and flies in the teeth of Article 267,” he said.

He further argued that consistency demands presidential candidates and running mates be treated identically under the law. “You cannot accord a presidential candidate a right to resign or withdraw but deny the same right to their running mate, as that amounts to discrimination and, to some extent, exploitation and forced labour. This position too has to be changed,” Chirwa said.

The warning adds to a growing body of legal commentary questioning the practical workability of the court’s position, with implications that extend beyond the current election cycle into how future presidential tickets are structured and challenged.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 4, 2026
World.content:
DR Congo Audit Confirms Oil Pollution Findings

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ministry of Hydrocarbons expects to complete and publish a full environmental audit of oil company Perenco by the end of September. This comes after preliminary findings that identified pollution linked to the company's operations. A ministry official said the audit found negative impacts on soil and air quality, with ageing infrastructure and pipelines contributing to environmental damage. The findings broadly support a recent Human Rights Watch report alleging that Perenco's activities, including gas flaring, open burning of oil waste and oil spills, have polluted air, soil and water sources and posed health risks to nearby communities. Perenco has denied causing pollution. However, the government said that the final report will recommend environmental remediation measures and infrastructure upgrades.

Benin Launches New Senate Chamber

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Benin has launched its new Senate, a second chamber of parliament designed to beef up legislative oversight and protect the country's constitutional order. The Senate will scrutinise laws, request second readings of bills and has the power to block constitutional, electoral and political party reforms it deems a danger to democracy, peace or national unity. It can also suspend or revoke the political rights of public officials accused of undermining state institutions or social cohesion. Supporters say the chamber will provide better checks and balances and preserve Benin's democratic traditions. Its legitimacy has been challenged by critics, who warn that, because its members are appointed, not directly elected, it could undermine democratic accountability.

AI-Enabled Cybercrime on the Rise Across Africa

More than half of all reported cybercrimes across Africa are now powered by artificial intelligence, according to INTERPOL's 2026 African Cyberthreat Assessment Report. The report found that 55% of reported cybercrime incidents involved AI-enabled tools. Cybercrime is becoming increasingly automated and transnational, with financial losses across the continent more than doubling since 2024 to an estimated $484 million, the report said. The most common threat remains online scams, where criminals are increasingly using AI-generated synthetic identities to bypass biometric security systems and commit fraud. INTERPOL also highlighted the growing threat of phishing, ransomware and mobile money fraud, calling on governments and businesses to shore up cybersecurity as organised criminal networks exploit AI to mount faster and more sophisticated attacks across Africa.

Zimbabwe's Examination Board Releases June 2026 Exam Results

The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has announced the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results. Candidates are able to access them online via the ZIMSEC portal. The Ordinary Level pass rate for candidates who wrote five or more subjects fell to 3%, down from 5.87% in 2025. The Advanced Level pass rate for candidates passing at least two subjects rose by 11.88% points to 67.74%. ZIMSEC said the online results portal will remain open for five days. Printed results will be available for collection by examination centre heads from regional offices.

Close 

UN Opens Major Ebola Treatment Centre in DR Congo

The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing its largest-ever Ebola outbreak. The virus has spread to 49 health zones across several provinces, with Ituri accounting for the vast majority of infections and deaths. In response, the United Nations and its partners are opening the country's largest Ebola treatment centre, with a capacity of 100 beds, alongside a new transit centre to improve early detection and referrals. WHO has warned that a major scale-up of response efforts is urgently needed. They cite conflict, displacement, cross-border movement and worsening humanitarian conditions as key factors driving the rapid spread of the disease.

World.title: South Africa: Water Crisis Turns Deadly in Durban - South African News Briefs - August 4, 2026
World.content:
Water Crisis Turns Deadly in Durban

Residents of Adams Mission, south of Durban, have accused government water tanker drivers of selling water that should be supplied free of charge, following the death of 43-year-old Celani Zungu, reports EWN. Community members allege Zungu was trying to stop a tanker from leaving without delivering water to residents when he was struck and killed by the vehicle. Local councillor Thembelihle Makhanya said there is no concrete evidence of water being sold. He condemned the allegations if proven true. Police are investigating a case of culpable homicide, while the eThekwini Municipality has launched an internal investigation.

Westbury Residents March Against Gang Violence

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Residents of Westbury in Johannesburg are set to march, demanding decisive action to curb persistent gang violence and drug-related crime, reports SABC News. Community leader Bishop Dulton Adams said residents are calling for long-term solutions rather than temporary police deployments. He argued that law enforcement has a lack of a visible presence in the neighbourhood. He criticised authorities for failing to patrol the area adequately and urged stronger policing and sustained interventions to tackle gangsterism.

Parliament Defends GBVF Council Picks

Parliament's Portfolio Committee on Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities has defended its recommendations for the newly appointed Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) Council, rejecting criticism from COSATU over the absence of a labour representative, reports EWN. Committee chairperson Liezl van der Merwe said the selection process was fair, legally compliant and based on candidates' experience and expertise. COSATU maintains the council should include organised labour and plans to challenge the appointments. Parliament has said that legal advice confirms that labour representation is not a legislative requirement under the GBVF Act.

More South African news

World.title: Somalia: Cabinet Officials Brace to Relinquish Kenyan Passports After Presidential Ultimatum
World.content:
A mounting cohort of senior Somali government ministers is poised to surrender their Kenyan passports and national identity documents within days, heeding President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's ultimatum that dual citizens holding public office must forswear their foreign nationality or immediately vacate their posts, according to multiple informed sources.

The impending wave of surrenders represents the most aggressive enforcement of citizenship integrity standards within the executive branch in recent memory, building on Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdirashid Haji's unilateral decision to return his Kenyan travel documents,a move that effectively set a binding precedent for his cabinet colleagues.

Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdirashid Haji became the first senior figure to bow to the directive when he formally handed over his Kenyan passport to the Kenyan Embassy in Mogadishu earlier this week.

In a terse statement, Jibril asserted the move was designed to guarantee "complete transparency" in the execution of his official duties and to preempt any challenge to his national allegiance.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Sources who spoke to Dalsan on condition of anonymity, citing lack of authorisation to engage publicly on the matter, disclosed that several ministers and state ministers are now finalising arrangements to submit their Kenyan travel credentials and identification cards to the diplomatic mission. The sources indicated that the officials are acting with haste to avoid being perceived as defying the President's edict, which was first articulated during a closed-door cabinet sitting last Thursday.

"The President made it unequivocally clear that retaining a foreign passport while occupying a senior government portfolio is untenable," one source told Dalsan. "Those who intend to retain their cabinet seats are moving swiftly to comply, and a series of handovers is widely anticipated before the week concludes."

The directive has cast a harsh glare on the prevalence of dual citizenship among Somalia's political elite--a sensitive issue long left unaddressed but now thrust into the open.

Although Somalia's provisional constitution does not explicitly outlaw dual nationality for public officials, the President's order effectively imposes a new litmus test for the upper echelons of power, compelling officials to choose definitively between their Somali responsibilities and foreign entitlements.

The enforcement drive comes against the backdrop of heightened scrutiny of senior officials' travel documentation, with some figures having recently encountered obstacles at Kenyan ports of entry.

Close 

State Minister at the Presidency Abdirashid was among those reportedly turned away by Kenyan immigration authorities, although it remains unclear whether that incident directly precipitated the presidential directive.

Villa Somalia has yet to issue a formal communiqué on the enforcement timeline, and the Kenyan government has likewise refrained from commenting on the expected influx of surrendered documents. However, insiders suggest the list of compliant officials will expand as the President's unannounced deadline looms, with further developments expected imminently.

World.title: West Africa: Ecowas Pledges U.S.$250,000 for June 29 Flood Victims
World.content:
THE Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has pledged US$250,000, equivalent to about GH¢3 million, to support victims of the June 29 floods that ravaged parts of Ghana.

The donation, announced by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Mr Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, is expected to bolster ongoing relief efforts for thousands of people affected by the disaster.

In a Facebook post, Mr Ablakwa said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had received official notification from the ECOWAS Commission on the assistance.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said the funds would be transferred in full to the appropriate state institutions immediately after they are received by the ministry.

Related Articles

"The transfer will be done in the interest of transparency and accountability," the minister assured.

Mr Ablakwa expressed the government's gratitude to ECOWAS for the gesture, describing it as a demonstration of solidarity and genuine African compassion at a difficult time for the country.

The June 29 floods affected communities in seven regions, claiming lives, displacing thousands of residents and destroying homes, roads and other infrastructure.

Government agencies, supported by humanitarian organisations and other stakeholders, have since been providing relief to affected families while efforts continue to restore livelihoods in the flood-hit communities.

The ECOWAS support is expected to complement the government's ongoing response to the disaster and bring relief to victims.

The June 29 floods, triggered by hours of torrential rainfall, submerged several communities across seven regions, including Greater Accra, causing widespread destruction to homes, businesses, roads and other public infrastructure.

The disaster claimed several lives, displaced thousands of residents and left many households stranded, with emergency response teams undertaking rescue operations while government agencies and humanitarian organisations provided relief items to affected families.

President John Dramani Mahama subsequently visited some of the worst-hit communities, describing the situation as a national tragedy and assuring victims of government's commitment to provide immediate relief and support reconstruction efforts.

Close 

The ECOWAS intervention is expected to complement ongoing government and humanitarian assistance aimed at easing the plight of affected families and supporting the recovery of flood-hit communities.

World.title: Uganda: 14 Killed As Truck Crashes Into Taxi in Lwera
World.content:
At least 14 people have been confirmed dead in a grisly accident in Lwera swamp along the Kampala -Masaka Highway.

The accident according to Greater Masaka Regional Police spokesperson, Twaha Kasirye, happened at around 11pm on Monday at Kamunga Trading Centre in Lwera Swamp, Kalungu District.

"The accident involved a Toyota Hiace taxi (UA 662AQ) and a Sino truck (UBS 040F) transporting sand. Fourteen (14) people died on the spot, all from the taxi," Kasirye said.

He added that four other people, including two occupants from each vehicle, sustained injuries and were rushed to Masaka Regional Referral Hospital, where they are currently receiving treatment.



He said police officers visited and documented the scene, while investigations into the cause of the crash are ongoing.

"Investigations are underway as efforts to trace the fleeing driver are ongoing."

The development comes as concerns over fatalities on Ugandan roads continue.

At least 37 people died in major road accidents within 10 days in July 2026, with four major crashes involving public transport vehicles, including three school buses carrying learners on educational trips and one passenger service bus.

The deadliest incident occurred on July 17 in Kapchorwa District, where 21 people, including 20 pupils of King David Junior School in Ndejje, Kampala, and one adult, died after their bus crashed while returning from a study tour at Sipi Falls.

The Isuzu bus, registration number UA 108BQ, reportedly developed mechanical problems before the fatal crash at Chekwatit Village, Kimawa Parish, Kawowo Sub-county.

Police preliminary investigations indicated that the driver lost control of the vehicle, which veered off the road, struck a large stone and overturned.

The tragedy raised concerns over the safety checks conducted before school trips and whether vehicles transporting learners meet the required safety standards.

Days earlier, on July 7, 2026, another fatal crash at Bobi Trading Centre along the Kampala-Gulu Highway claimed 14 lives and left 28 others injured.

The crash involved a passenger bus, registration number UBE 110H, belonging to OPIT Travellers Company, and a Mercedes-Benz Actros trailer, registration numbers KBS 564D/ZE 7948.

According to police findings, the bus driver was speeding and lost control while attempting to avoid a pedestrian crossing the road, resulting in a head-on collision with the trailer.

The police annual traffic report for 2025 indicated that Uganda registered 26,044 road crashes, indicating a 3.7% increase from the figure registered in 2024.

Close 

Of these, 4,602 were fatal, rising from the 4,434 reported in 2024 while 18,444 people got serious injuries and 3,668 got minor injuries.

In the accidents, men accounted for 83% of all the deaths while October with 523 deaths registered the highest fatalities.

World.title: South Africa: Anger After Farmers Dump Rotting Fruit Near Homes
World.content:
Farmers would never do this in their own suburbs, say Eastern Cape residents

Residents of Patensie, Eastern Cape, say farmers dumped truckloads of rotting fruit, nets and other farm waste on land earmarked for a housing project.

Kouga Local Municipality removed 14 truckloads of waste and says the illegal dumping has been referred to law enforcement for investigation.

Acht Boerdery says it has a longstanding arrangement to provide waste fruit for animals and denies dumping the nets and cables. Waterwiel Boerdery says it only left flood-damaged netting at the site after people requested it, and has since removed the material. Quacha Boerdery did not respond.

Residents of Patensie in the Eastern Cape have accused farmers of dumping truckloads of oranges and lemons, as well as farm equipment on land near their homes. They say farmers "would never do this in their own suburbs".

The rotting fruit attracted insects, as well as pigs and cattle, and created a heavy stench over Ramaphosa Village. Meanwhile, discarded nets, cables and irrigation pipes littered the site.



The Kouga Local Municipality has cleared the area, removing 14 truckloads of waste.

The open land in Stuurmanskop is earmarked for a housing project.

Community leader Eric Blaauw posted on the What's Happening in Patensie Facebook page on 19 July: "New illegal dumping site by our farmers around Patensie. This is not good at all for the health and safety of our kids. This area is for housing development, not dumping. We're really being undermined."

Ward 10 councillor Mbandana Msingathi Gerald said he was alerted on 19 July to complaints about the stench from rotten lemons. Residents accused Acht Boerdery and Quacha Boerdery of dumping the fruit.

"I contacted local farmers' association chairperson Grewar Oosthuizen and gave him the names of the alleged dumpers. He promised to act immediately. Nets, wires and irrigation pipes were scattered across roads in Ramaphosa Village," Gerald said.

He said cattle ate the oranges but not the lemons.

Residents had previously buried fruit and vegetables at the site, but this stopped once the site was designated for housing.

Gerald said Patensie's only dumping site closed a year ago. Residents now have to travel 15km to Hankey to dispose of waste, and many cannot afford it. He said there is no local transit site, which is a serious issue for a town that exports fruit internationally.

Kouga Local Municipality spokesperson Monique Basson said officials had acted immediately after seeing reports on social media.

Basson told GroundUp: "We removed 14 truckloads of waste. The waste management section conducted a site inspection which confirmed illegal dumping.

"The matter was referred to law enforcement for investigation with the aim of identifying those responsible and taking legal action in terms of municipal by-laws," she said.

Acht Boerdery director Christof Opperman said the farm had a longstanding arrangement with the local livestock farmers' committee and the councillor's office to provide waste product for cattle, pigs, goats and chickens in an area where the animals already graze.

Opperman said recent floods and market pressure linked to the conflict in the Middle East had affected export and juicing channels, leaving fruit it believed still suitable for livestock.

"We also use the Hankey municipal dump for other waste and were not advised that the livestock product was excessive," he said.

Opperman said the farm was not involved in dumping the nets and cables. "We remain committed to sustainable farming and would not knowingly endanger the community, its people or its animals."

Opperman said staff may take waste fruit home for personal use and for their livestock, while remaining waste fruit is taken to the agreed grazing area and residual waste is mulched.

Close 

Charl Malan of Waterwiel Boerdery said his farm only dropped off flood-damaged covering nets at the site after people requested them. He denied dumping any fruit.

"After the floods, people asked me for netting that was damaged. After it was dropped off in heaps, it was scattered around by people taking the nets. I was unaware that fruit was dumped there. That must have happened afterwards and was not done by me," Malan said.

Malan said he did not anticipate the netting would become a health hazard.

Malan said the farm regularly experiences vandalism and theft. He said he hoped giving away damaged netting would reduce theft from the farm.

Malan said that as soon as he became aware of the problem, he sent his own workers and machinery to remove the netting. GroundUp saw workers using one of Malan's tractors to collect the nets.

Quacha Boerdery did not respond to requests for comment.

World.title: Zimbabwe: ZIMSEC Releases 2026 June Exam Results - O-Level Pass Rate Drops, A-Level Performance Improves
World.content:
The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has announced the release of the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results, with candidates able to access them online from 6pm Monday.

The Ordinary Level pass rate for candidates who wrote five or more subjects fell by 2.87%, from 5.87% recorded in 2025, to 3% in June 2026.

The Advanced Level pass rate for candidates who passed at least two subjects (Grade E or better) increased by 11.88% from last year, to 67.74% in 2026.

Speaking during a media briefing in Harare, ZIMSEC board chairperson Professor Paul Mapfumo said the results would be available on the examination body's online portal for only five days.

"The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council board and management would like to advise the nation of the release of the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results.

"With effect from today, 3 August 2026 at 6pm, Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results will be accessible to all candidates and authorised personnel online through the ZIMSEC portal accessed via the ZIMSEC website.

"Please take note that this portal will be open for five days only," said Mapfumo.

Mapfumo also said heads of examination centres would begin collecting printed results for their respective schools and centres from ZIMSEC regional offices on Tuesday.

World.title: Africa: Over Half of Africa's Cybercrimes Are AI-Enabled - Interpol
World.content:
Nairobi — More than half of all cybercrimes reported across Africa are now AI-enabled, the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) has revealed, warning that digital attacks have rapidly evolved into an industrialized, borderless ecosystem that is becoming increasingly difficult to detect and combat.

According to the newly released INTERPOL African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026, 55 percent of cybercrimes reported across the continent now involve Artificial Intelligence (AI), underscoring a major shift in the cyber threat landscape.

The report says cybercrime has evolved into an increasingly automated underground economy, where criminal networks are using AI and other advanced technologies to launch attacks faster, at greater scale, and across multiple countries simultaneously.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The report further shows that cybercrime-related financial losses across Africa have more than doubled since 2024, reaching an estimated $484 million.

The assessment, based on survey data from 36 member countries and intelligence from private sector partners including Fortinet, Mastercard, the Shadowserver Foundation, S2W and TrendAI, found that 72 percent of surveyed countries reported the presence of organized scam centres, with the highest concentration in Southern and West Africa.

Among the most alarming developments highlighted in the report is the growing use of AI-generated synthetic identities to bypass biometric security systems.

Criminals are combining stolen personal information with fabricated data to deceive identity verification processes, enabling them to open bank accounts, obtain mobile loans and register SIM cards under false identities.

Online scams remain the most frequently reported form of cybercrime across the continent, while the financial services, telecommunications and government sectors continue to bear the brunt of AI-enabled credential theft and automated social engineering attacks.

The findings mirror Kenya's own evolving cyber threat landscape.

In June, the Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) announced that it detected 3.37 billion cyber threat events between January and March 2026. Although this represented a 26.15 percent decline from the previous quarter, the authority cautioned that attacks had become increasingly sophisticated, with system attacks targeting critical information infrastructure accounting for 3.23 billion of the incidents.

The INTERPOL report also noted that Kenya ranked among SOCRadar's top phishing detections globally in September 2025.

Recent cyber incidents have further illustrated the growing risks facing the country. One notable case occurred on July 18, 2026, when hackers compromised the official website of the President William Ruto, defacing its homepage with messages targeting President Ruto and demanding a ransom of five Bitcoins, worth about Sh41 million at the time.

The attackers threatened to leak unspecified information if their demands were not met. The government immediately took the website offline, with Information, Communications and the Digital Economy Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo assuring the public that response protocols had been activated and that there was no evidence of unauthorized access to sensitive government data. The presidential website was restored two days later.

The growing sophistication of cyberattacks has prompted coordinated international operations aimed at dismantling transnational cybercrime networks.

Under Operation Red Card 2.0, conducted between December 8, 2025, and January 30, 2026, across 16 African countries, law enforcement agencies arrested 651 suspects and recovered more than USD 4.3 million. Investigators identified 1,247 victims, whose reported losses exceeded USD 45 million.

In Kenya, authorities arrested 27 individuals linked to online investment fraud schemes that relied on messaging applications, social media platforms and fabricated testimonials to lure victims.

Investigators said suspects convinced victims to make initial investments of as little as USD 50, displaying fake investment dashboards showing fictitious profits before blocking withdrawals and disappearing with the funds.

A separate global operation, Operation Synergia III, conducted between July 18, 2025, and January 31, 2026, brought together law enforcement agencies from 72 countries and territories.

The operation resulted in the takedown of more than 45,000 malicious servers and internet addresses linked to phishing, ransomware and information-stealing malware campaigns, while leading to 94 key arrests worldwide.

"Cybercrime in 2026 is more sophisticated and destructive than ever before, but Operation Synergia III stands as a powerful testament to what global cooperation can achieve," said Neal Jetton, Director of INTERPOL's Cybercrime Directorate.

Jetton said organized cybercriminal syndicates continue to inflict severe financial and psychological harm on individuals, businesses and communities through increasingly sophisticated online fraud schemes, emphasizing that Operation Red Card demonstrates the critical role of international collaboration in combating transnational cybercrime.

Close 

The report also highlights significant regional variations in cyber threats. East Africa has emerged as a hotspot for mobile money fraud and ransomware attacks targeting critical infrastructure, while West and Central Africa remain major centres for business email compromise and romance scams.

Southern Africa continues to attract global threat actors seeking to maximize disruption due to its high levels of digital connectivity.

Meanwhile, cybersecurity partner TrendAI recorded approximately 600,000 detections linked to AI-generated deepfakes, digital sextortion and other forms of synthetic media abuse.

As cybercriminals increasingly harness AI to automate attacks and expand their operations across borders, INTERPOL is urging governments, businesses and individual users to strengthen cybersecurity awareness, verify digital communications before acting on them, and safeguard personal information against an increasingly sophisticated and rapidly evolving cyber threat landscape.

World.title: Reporter's Notebook: Inside the Senate showdown over Trump's push to scrap August recess
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

"Should I stay or should I go now? If I go there will be trouble. And if I stay it will be double." – The Clash

The words "schedule" and "Congress" don’t always mesh.

But the formal Senate schedule has long had senators taking off at the end of this week until early September for the customary "August recess."

Only thing is, President Trump and some conservatives pushing for approval of the SAVE America Act don’t want the Senate to beg off. They assert that the Senate should remain in session until it passes the bill, which requires proof of citizenship to vote.

"I think there’s nothing more important than they pass the SAVE America Act. I think they should stay," said President Trump. "They do what they want. But I think they should stay."

SEN RICK SCOTT: AMERICANS WORK FIVE DAYS A WEEK, WHY CAN’T THE SENATE?

The Senate has already defeated two efforts to adopt the SAVE America Act. So there’s not an obvious pathway to alter those previous outcomes. Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., has rebuffed the President’s demands to stay in session.

"I don’t think having a Congress sitting around here for the month of August and quorum calls or having to vote on Democrat amendments is probably a good use of anybody's time," said Thune.

There’s tension between the South Dakota Republican and the President over the Senate’s legislative realities. Thune may be Majority Leader. But Thune believes the President bears responsibility for changing some minds on Capitol Hill.

"We have in the past suggested to he and his team to come up here and visit with some of my Republican colleagues," said Thune. "Now if he can change the facts and start moving some of those senators who are noes into yesses, then we have a different conversation. But that's just the reality."

As always, it’s about the math. And the SAVE America Act lacks the votes.

"I know Sen. Thune says the votes aren't there. I'm not saying he's wrong. I'm just saying people change their mind sometimes," argued Sen. John Kennedy, R-La.

But it doesn’t look like there will even be a vote on that, unless something ripens quickly.

That’s where Sens. Mike Lee, R-Utah, Ted Cruz, R-Texas, Roger Marshall, R-Kas, Rick Scott, R-Fla., and others have suggested the Senate shouldn’t go on break unless they pass the bill.

So what happens next?

Let’s say we get to Friday night. The Senate has taken its final vote of the summer. Maybe to confirm Todd Blanche as Attorney General. Perhaps the measure named after late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., which sanctions Russia. The Senate is ready to finish until mid-September. In recent years, the Senate has not voted on a resolution to go out of session for weeks on end. That’s where SAVE America Act proponents would attempt to block such an effort. But its immaterial since there is no vote.

In the not too distant past, the House and Senate often approved "adjournment resolutions." But not right now. Such a plan must align with the wishes of the House of Representatives. Article I, Section 6 of the Constitution bars either body for adjourning for more than three days "without the Consent of the other." The House isn’t around to approve an adjournment resolution. It’s been out of session for a couple of weeks now. Moreover, it’s not clear that the House could adopt an adjournment resolution.

So, under the Constitution, each body must - at a minimum - hold a brief "pro forma" session where lawmakers convene for just a few seconds and then immediately gavel out. That meets the Constitutional requirement.

But there’s the rub.

When the Senate wraps up, Thune or one of his lieutenants would usually go to the floor and ask "unanimous consent" that the Senate meet on a series of Mondays and Thursdays or Tuesdays and Fridays between now and September. These are the "pro forma" sessions, convening at three-day intervals. But if Lee or someone wants to object, they’re stuck. The Senate can’t green light the set of pro formas. The Senate must have buy-in of all 100 senators.

REPUBLICAN SAYS TRUMP'S TOP ELECTION PRIORITY 'DEAD' IN SENATE AS GOP FRACTURES AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

But an objection in this case hardly blocks the recess or compels debate – let alone a vote or passage – on the SAVE America Act.

If Thune or his designee can’t get unanimous consent, the only option they have is to move to meet again the next day. Let’s say 9 a.m. ET. If someone objects to the time, it will meet at noon et under the Senate’s default protocols.

That said, this is where someone could force what might constitute the de facto "vote to go on recess." A Republican senator might demand a vote on the Senate adjourning for the day on Friday and meeting on Saturday. This is not a vote to "go on recess." But it’s the closest someone can engineer a possible vote related to Senate action.

A motion to adjourn is not debatable on the floor. But it is amendable. Someone could offer another option about when the Senate should meet. But that’s about it.

On this hypothetical Saturday session, it’s possible that Thune could simply get recognition and ask for the Senate to adjourn for the day again. One of those pushing the SAVE America Act doesn’t even get recognized to speak. However, if Thune is gracious and is willing to allow someone to have their say, they could get the floor and hold it as long as they want.

Note that doing so does not constitute a filibuster. Filibusters are efforts by senators to stop something. In this case, advocates of the SAVE America Act are trying to start something. So no filibuster. This would just be a really long speech. But Thune might not let it come to that. And even though they’ve chattered about it a lot, the strongest advocates of the SAVE America Act have not taken advantage of their prerogatives as senators and gone down to hold the floor at length.

Keep in mind that SAVE America Act advocates could potentially do this and push for recognition on the floor on all subsequent days during the August recess. Thune could block them from speaking because the order of the day is to convene and adjourn during a pro forma session. And if the SAVE America Act faction were to push for a vote, all it takes is another senator to block them on the floor.

One might ask the question about whether the SAVE America Act group might demand a "live" quorum call (where all senators must report to the floor for attendance) or even the more extreme motion of "instructing the Sergeant at Arms to arrest" absent senators and bring them to the floor. Well, this works at cross purposes during August. The reason? The Senate doesn’t have a quorum. In the old days, the Senate took quorum calls to establish if enough senators present were present to do business. It violates the Constitution to conduct business without a quorum present.

The SAVE America Act coalition may prove that there aren’t enough senators in Washington to conduct business. That helps make their point. But it also forces the Senate to adjourn because it can’t operate without a quorum.

WATCH: DEMOCRATS ADMIT WHEN THEY'D ELIMINATE THE FILIBUSTER AS SAVE ACT FIGHT HEATS UP

These gambits might not achieve the legislative goal of passing the SAVE America Act. But there are other benefits for SAVE America Act advocates. A series of lengthy speeches could potentially delay the recess. These Republican senators could argue that they are willing to stay and debate the SAVE America Act while their colleagues fled Washington for summer. Such a maneuver would focus attention on the issue. It would draw a contrast between senators willing to fight for the issue and those who went home. The effort might impress President Trump. And such a maneuver could show divides between them and Thune – who the President often chastises.

But pass the SAVE America Act? It’s not going to do that. And some Republican senators emphasize the importance of taking a few weeks off so their colleagues can campaign.

"The worst case scenario is for us is to stay all the way through and then we lose the Senate in the days ahead," said Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., on Fox. "Then President Trump is dealing with all the impeachment crazy all over again."

Remaining in Washington for the next five weeks would pull the most vulnerable GOP senator off the trail, Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine.

Collins was crystal clear when pressed by yours truly whether she would campaign and miss her first roll call vote since entering the Senate in 1997.

"I don’t miss votes," said an emphatic Collins.

So don’t expect the Senate to forgo the recess at the end of the week.

In fact, a decision by the Senate to go on recess may even work to the political advantage of those pushing for the SAVE America Act. They can then rail against Thune’s leadership and their colleagues for not passing the bill. Again, they don’t score the legislative outcome. But they sure rack up some political points.

This is why those philosopher kings who comprise the band the The Clash may have been on to something. If the Senate stays, Republicans can’t pass the SAVE America Act. But if they go, certain GOP senators can rabble rouse.

There’s trouble whether senators stay or go.

World.title: Chicago White Sox lead American League Central but face a red-hot Boston Red Sox team Tuesday
World.content:
With the trade deadline passing Monday, we are officially on playoff watch for teams. Every game from here on will take on a bit more intensity and importance. We know a few teams have dropped out of the race after the trades that took place. Others bolstered their roster, and we have two of them that are going all in, taking each other on today as the White Sox face the Red Sox.

It is the start of August, and the Chicago White Sox are leading the American League Central. Now, before you put a reservation down for some playoff tickets, keep in mind that the Tigers were leading the division to start August last year, and they were heavy favorites to win it. The problem is that the Guardians were lurking, had a spectacular September, and took down the AL Central. The Tigers still made the postseason, but it feels like we will get two Wild Card teams from the American League East, so the safest path for the White Sox is to win the division.

They did add to the team at the trade deadline, and that should instill a bit more confidence in the roster. Their rotation will now have a couple of dependable guys. Davis Martin is one of those guys, but he is approaching the most innings he's pitched in a year. He is 9-5 with a 3.62 ERA and a 1.26 WHIP. He struggled in July after a mixed bag of results in June, so you do need to wonder if his success is fading. The White Sox went 1-4 in his starts in July, and he allowed 16 earned runs in 24 innings. One of those games was against the Red Sox where he allowed five earned runs in four innings.

RED SOX COME BACK FROM THE DEAD, MOVE INTO POSTSEASON CONTENTION WITH REMARKABLE 14-GAME WIN STREAK

The Boston Red Sox made arguably the most shocking move of the trade deadline, by acquiring Adley Rutschman from the Baltimore Orioles. The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24. Since that point, they've gone 28-5. They have had three separate five-game or more winning streaks in that stretch, including one they are on right now. They just swept the Dodgers, arguably the best team in baseball. Can this level of winning be sustained for two more months? Unlikely, but it is impressive nonetheless.

Tuesday they send Patrick Sandoval to the hill in hopes of making it six games in a row. For the year, Sandoval only has four starts under his belt and carries a 3.32 ERA and a 1.58 WHIP. None of his starts have been ugly or bad by any means. He did allow four earned runs against the Rays, but the other three saw him allow two or fewer. He faced the White Sox in the first start of his season and went 4.1 innings and allowed just one earned run on five hits.

It is hard to pick against the Red Sox with how hot as they've been. I have faded them in a couple of spots, but it didn't work out. The additions from the deadline should rejuvenate both of these teams as well. I think we should take the hotter team today, and I think we also need to start fading Martin. He will probably still have some good starts left, but he has struggled lately. He also didn't have a great June. His arm might just be getting tired. I'll take Sandoval and the Red Sox on the moneyline tonight.

World.title: Battlefield robots open new front in innovation war with major US adversary
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

FIRST ON FOX: The U.S. Army is teaming up with an artificial intelligence (AI) company to build an AI "brain" for military robots that can think, understand their surroundings and continue missions even after losing contact with human operators as the race for AI dominance intensifies.

Working with the Army Research Laboratory, defense AI company EdgeRunner AI has developed an onboard AI system that allows military robots to function in the battlefield without relying on cloud computing or an internet connection in environments where connectivity is lost.

"We like to think of robots as the next frontier of AI," EdgeRunner AI founder and CEO Tyler Saltsman told Fox News Digital.

"Think of them as a very far-out edge device, kind of like a cell phone, a tablet or a laptop. But now what we can do is we can put a brain, or a neural network, right on that robot so that robots can have context when they're on a mission helping the warfighter."

CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE

The partnership comes as the U.S. and China race to integrate AI into their militaries, with both countries viewing AI as critical to maintaining a technological edge in future conflicts.

Saltsman said it's important for the U.S. to stay ahead in the global AI race, calling China's dominance in drone manufacturing "problematic."

"Whether or not China's ahead of us is debatable, but if China is, it's not by much," he said.

Saltsman said today's AI is "too generalized," which is why his company is developing technology built for specific military missions.

"Warfighters don't need 19th-century poetry," he said. "They need specific intelligence to his or her occupation in order to make better decisions in the heat of battle and that can increase the probability of winning the fight."

Working alongside aerial drones, the AI is designed to help robots "problem solve through different routes" while detecting explosives, carrying ammunition, scouting routes and reporting enemy activity.

UKRAINE’S BATTLEFIELD IS TRANSFORMING THE FUTURE OF NATO

"As you combine them together, you get a much better clarity of the battlefield and increased situational awareness," he said.

When communications are cut off, Saltsman said the military will need autonomous systems that can continue making decisions on their own.

"You can have a human pilot that controls the ground robot or the drone in the air," he said. "But then if they were to be jammed by a radar jammer and lose connectivity, then the neural network on that robot can still continue the mission and still aid the warfighter."

Saltsman argued the military "can't rely on internet access in war," warning that depending on systems like SpaceX's Starlink could add a "risk" to missions.

"The problem with Starlink is if you use it, you're effectively showing the enemy where you are, so you might as well be wearing a beacon on you saying, 'Hey, here's where I'm located,'" he said.

INSIDE CHINA’S AI ‘WOLF PACK’ DRONES BUILT WITH TAIWAN CONFLICT IN MIND

Pointing to the Russia-Ukraine war, Saltsman said the success of drones has sparked a new push for autonomous ground robots.

"As drones have become ubiquitous, now ground robots are like the next thing and then eventually humanoid robots so robots that move and look like humans," he said.

Despite the push to advance military AI, Saltsman said safety can't take a back seat and that the technology is built using "transparent" datasets to "understand the biases" of the AI.

"That's another thing that differentiates us," he said. "One of the problems is how to use AI safely, how to put guardrails around it and how to understand it."

While the technology remains in the "development phase," Saltsman said the breakthrough gives robots the ability to understand what they see, not just detect it.

"You can put computer vision models on robots so they can see, but if they don't understand the context of what they're seeing, they're not useful and that's what we're solving for."

World.title: Post-trade deadline futures bets worth taking on the World Series and division winners
World.content:
The trade deadline is now behind us, and we had a flurry of deals yesterday. As a sports bettor, it is important to pay attention to this information. Not only does it signify that some teams are going to start (or further continue) tanking. It also means we probably need to reevaluate the teams and even some of our future positions. I don't normally look at a ton of baseball futures because it takes too long for them to pay off, but there might be some opportunity for us to grab value on some bets before the season ends.

World Series Champion

The Los Angeles Dodgers are still the overwhelming favorites to win the World Series. They are +160 to win it now. Can you imagine having to face Tarik Skubal, then Yoshinobu Yamamoto, then Blake Snell, then Tyler Glasnow, then Shohei Ohtani as a rotation in a seven-game series? It is rather absurd. However, there is no value remaining at +160. The Red Sox were major players at the deadline, but they didn't get much better in their rotation. I just don't see the pitching to get it done. The Chicago Cubs at 15:1 might actually have what it takes to get past the Dodgers. They just so happen to play each other tonight, with Skubal's debut coming. The Cubs added Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes to their rotation, and that should - as long as they don't suffer more injuries - give them solid enough pitching to navigate a lot of series. Another National League team that I like is the Padres at +7500.

The Padres did not fold as some people expected. Instead, they went out and addressed their starting pitching needs. They were able to get Robbie Ray (a former Cy Young winner), and they also grabbed Casey Mize from the Tigers. Their hitting has been down, but you would think some of their guys will come back to their normal averages. At this value, I think you have to take them. The Phillies at +1800 added a guy in Luis Arraez who will be on base, and Zack Wheeler and Christopher Sanchez give them a chance against anyone.

In the American League, I like the Mariners, who addressed their biggest need by acquiring Taylor Ward from the Orioles. They are at +2200 and should have the best rotation in the playoffs, but they need to make it there first. The Rays are +1300 and one of the best teams in baseball. They will have a great 1-2 punch in Shane McClanahan and Freddy Peralta.

Worst Team

Fellow writer, Geoff Clark, took the Angels to be the worst team in baseball this season before the year began. He got them at +2200, so he has excellent value. They are now +145 to have the fewest wins, and they have two fewer than anyone in baseball. They traded away a lot of guys, kept their young talent, and acquired guys that could actually help later. I think even at +145 you're looking at a good ticket. The only issue is that the Angels play in the worst division in baseball while the Rockies play in one of the better ones. The Athletics have just two more wins than the Angels and are also tanking. Assuming both play their division down the stretch, the Rockies (+135) could lose more games.

Division Winners

The Rays are -120 to win the American League East with a 3.5 game lead over the Yankees and 5.5 over the Red Sox. If you're going to take someone in this division, take one of them at plus money. The Red Sox have been the hottest team in baseball for about a month now, and are +475.

I really like the Guardians to win the AL Central at +200. They are three games behind a good, but very young White Sox team. Chicago added some key pieces, especially Luis Castillo. However, the Guardians also traded for some good additions like Foster Griffin. The Guardians seemingly do this every year. I like them to take the division even with the Twins also chasing.

The Mariners still have the best team in the division on paper and are now +180 to win the division. Their rotation is easily the best, and Ward might push their offense into a gear they've been missing this season. Give me the Mariners.

There really aren't any divisions worth talking about in the National League. The Braves, Brewers, and Dodgers are all massive favorites. The Brewers are the only one that I could see slipping, but I don't think it is worth a bet.

For me, I'll put in a bet on the Cubs at +1500 to win the World Series, the Padres at +7500, and the Mariners at +2200. I'll also take the Guardians and Mariners to win their divisions. The trade deadline is done, but our betting on baseball has a long way to go!

World.title: Moscow and Kyiv trade blame over drone explosion that killed 7, including 3 children, on Russian beach
World.content:
The beach was packed, many vacationers lounging near the turquoise waters when the drone slammed into the white sand and burst into a fireball.

Russian officials said seven people, including three children, were killed and 58 others injured by the explosion in the Black Sea resort town of Gelendzhik on Monday. The explosion was captured on video and shared on social media, and verified by NBC News.

Moscow accused Ukraine of targeting civilians, which would constitute a war crime, and unleashed a barrage of aerial strikes on its neighbor. Ukraine’s attacks inside Russia come as its own civilians faced deadly Russian bombardment throughout the summer.

Ukrainian officials did not confirm they were responsible, but they also did not deny it.

“What happened today was a deliberate strike by the Kyiv regime against the civilian population — people who have absolutely no connection to military infrastructure,” Veniamin Kondratyev, the governor of the Krasnodar region, said on his official Telegram channel. “There can be no justification for such a cynical and inhumane terrorist act targeting children.”

A screen grab of a drone explosion on a beach at the holiday village of Arkhipo-Osipovka, Gelendzhik resort area, in Russia on Monday. via Reuters

The explosion comes amid a concerted Ukrainian effort to push the war’s front line closer than ever to Moscow, with strikes targeting shipping vessels, oil sites, warehouses and ammunition depots in recent weeks.

Since Russian President Vladimir Putin launched his large-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Kyiv has honed an innovative and lethal strategy of using cheaply manufactured drones as it seeks to pressure Moscow into a peace settlement. Some hit their targets, while others are often shot down.

Between July 24 and July 31, at least 61 people were killed and more than 320 wounded in Ukrainian shelling and drone strikes, Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said Friday.

After the explosion in Gelendzhik, Andriy Kovalenko, head of the Ukrainian National Security and Defense Council’s Centre for Countering Disinformation, said: “Russian air defense shot down a drone onto people lying on the beach.”

“It was Putin who killed these Russians,” he said in a statement. “Had he not started the war and the strikes on Ukraine, they would be alive.”

Kovalenko also accused Putin of downplaying Ukrainian attacks on Russia, creating an “illusion of peace” that has made the public complacent.

“Had they acknowledged the war on their own territory, people would have reacted more actively to the alert, which in some places in Russia is not even announced,” he said.

A separate attack had also hit a warehouse in Leningrad, its regional governor, Aleksandr Drozdenko, said early Tuesday.

World.title: Behind closed doors, Trump, White House aides hope Rep. Max Miller exits race
World.content:
Washington — Some White House officials hope embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller exits the congressional race in Ohio immediately, and President Trump has expressed a similar sentiment behind closed doors, multiple U.S. officials familiar with the matter tell CBS News.

Mr. Trump called Miller on Monday and raised concerns about his reelection bid following allegations that Miller assaulted his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and their 2-year-old daughter, two sources directly familiar with the call confirmed to CBS News. But Miller, who has adamantly denied the allegations, told the president he has no plans to leave the race, according to one of the sources.

Miller, the GOP nominee, has until 4 p.m. Wednesday to withdraw his candidacy and give Republicans a chance to replace him on the ballot in November. Semafor first reported that the president and some White House aides said privately that they wanted Miller out of the race.

On Tuesday morning, Miller said he would file the paperwork to launch a congressional ethics investigation into himself in an effort to clear his name.

"In light of all the renewed interest in my family affairs I am going to file my own paperwork for an ethics investigation into myself to clear my name from these horrific attacks on myself and family," Miller wrote on X. "I have absolutely nothing to hide. We will be providing the committee all necessary documents needed for a detail[ed] examination. The accusations continue to change, but my facts stay the same. I am looking forward to my colleagues reading everything for themselves."

On Monday, the president said he thought Miller was a "very good person" and said he would let the families involved resolve the situation.

"Well, it's a very sad thing," the president told reporters in the Oval Office Monday. "I know Max, he's a good person, I mean, I always thought he was a very good person. And I'm going to let the families figure that out. Those families, I know they're working on it. It's a very sad thing. Especially when you know somebody so well to be going through that. But it's accusations. And I'm going to let them figure that out."

In an earlier statement to CBS News on Monday, Miller said: "If I dropped out of this race, it would mean we as a nation have fallen so far from our American values. I will not validate false claims by removing myself just to please the court of public opinion. I am innocent of all of the allegations that have been attributed to me. I have done well representing my constituents' interests. Why would I drop out?"

Emily Moreno, Miller's ex-wife, is the daughter of Ohio GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno. The senator said in a statement on Sunday that Miller "should not serve in the House of Representatives" and "needs serious psychological help."
